title: Man Rati Vrindavan Sau Keejai - Shri Hariram Vyas, Vyas Vani, Purvardh (24)
sanskrit_text: Man Rati Vrindavan Sau Keejai.Khaayau Piyau Bharyau Bhoonjyau, Ab Jeevan Kau Phal Leejai. [1]Kaaj Akaash Jaani Sab Aapunau, Dau Sanvarau Deejai.Dekhi Dhenu Suni Bainu Rainu Taji, Dhrik-Dhrik Jag Jau Jeejai. [2]Jamuna Tat Vansivat Nikat, Rahat Joo Yah Tan Chhaijai.Varshat Shyamasyam Ras Ras, Vyas Nainan Bhari Peejai. [3]- Shri Hariram Vyas, Vyas Vani, Purvardh (24)Let your mind be lovingly immersed in Vrindavan. After satisfying worldly desires—eating, drinking, wandering, and enjoying—now receive life’s true fruit. [1]Understand what is truly meaningful and what is not, and now rectify your misfortune.Gaze upon the cows, hear the flute, feel the sacred dust of Vrindavan, and abandon all ties to the deceptive world. Live only for this divine purpose. [2]Reside near the bank of Yamuna at Vanshivat, and let this body perish there alone. The nectar of the maharaas of the divine couple, Sri Shyama Shyam, showers ceaselessly in Vrindavan. One may drink it fully with eyes immersed in love, says Hariram Vyas. [3]

title: Re Chitta Chintaya Chiram Vrishbhanuputrim - Shri Vagish Shastriji, Shri Radha Saptashati (7.67)
sanskrit_text: Re Chitta Chintaya Chiram Vrishbhanuputrim No Vismar Kshanamapiti Mamabhilashah.Radheti Naam Jap Bho Rasne Mamang Radhavane Vasa Tadangghrirjo Bhiliptam.- Shri Vagish Shastriji, Shri Radha Saptashati (7.67)O mind! Always contemplate Shri Radha, and never forget Her, not even for a moment. This is my heartfelt desire. O tongue! Keep chanting the sweet, nectar-like name “Radha.” O body! Be adorned with the sacred dust of Shri Radha’s lotus feet, and dwell forever in Her divine forest named Shri Vrindavan.

title: Jamuna Tat Syam Ghatani Ki Paanti - Shri Vitthal Vipul Dev Ju Ki Vani (28)
sanskrit_text: (Raag Malar)Jamuna Tat Syam Ghatani Ki Paanti.Harit Bhoomi Ban, Harit Sikhandi, Bolat Ati Ras Maanti. [1]Surang Choonari Ki Chhavi Dulahin, Abharan Nana Bhanti.Shribithalvipul Binod Bihari Son, Mili Vilasati Kilkaanti. [2] - Shri Vitthal Vipul Dev Ji, Shri Vitthal Vipul Dev Ju Ki Vani (28)Describing the charm of the monsoon season, Shrivipulbiharinidasi Ji says that dark rainclouds beautifully adorn the skies along the banks of Shri Yamuna Ji. The land and forest of Vrindavan have turned lush green, and peacocks sing joyfully, intoxicated by the rasa of the season. [1]The Eternal Bride, Shri Radha, is adorned with gorgeous colored chunari and various ornaments. Sri Vitthal Vipul Dev says, enchanted by the sweetness of the monsoon rasa, Sri Radha delights in playful pastimes with Her Beloved, Banke Bihariji, and revels in joyful, playful words. [2]

title: Bhoole Tain Kartaar Ke Raag Na Aavai Raas - Shri Rasnidhi
sanskrit_text: Bhoole Tain Kartaar Ke, Raag Na Aavai Raas.Yahi Samujh Kai Raakh Tu, Man Kartaarain Paas.- Shri RasnidhiIf a singer forgets the khartal, the rhythm of the raga collapses. Similarly, if the mind is disconnected from God and only the senses are engaged, bhakti loses its essence, and spiritual rasa cannot arise.

title: Jay Gahavar Kunj Nikunjan Ki - Braj Ke Sawaiya
sanskrit_text: (Sawaiya)Jay Gahavar Kunj Nikunjan Ki,Ras Prem Prakashini Shyama Ki Jay Jay. [1]Jay Daan Aur Maan Vilas Gadhi,Gahavar Van Rasik Samaj Ki Jay Jay. [2] Rasikeshvar Jahan Sakhi Bhesh Dharain,Un Mor Biharini Shyama Ki Jay Jay. [3]Ras Prem Ki Moorati Gopi Basen,Shridham Sadan Barsane Ki Jay Jay. [4]- Braj Ke SawaiyaGlory to the kuñjas and nikunjas of Gahvara vana in Barsanā, Glory to Śrī Rādhā, the illuminator of divine rasa and prema. [1]Glory to Dāṅgarh, Māṅgarh, and Vilāsgarh. Glory to the blissful gathering of rasikas in the Gahvara forest. [2]Glory to Mor Kuṭī, where Rasikeśvara Śrī Kṛṣṇa assumes the form of a sakhi (female companion), to please Mor Bihāriṇī Śrī Śyāmā Jū. [3]Where dwell the gopīs, embodiments of divine love and rasa—Endless glory to the sacred land of Barsānā. [4]

Glory to the blissful gathering of rasikas in the Gahvara forest. [2]Glory to Mor Kuṭī, where Rasikeśvara Śrī Kṛṣṇa assumes the form of a sakhi (female companion), to please Mor Bihāriṇī Śrī Śyāmā Jū. [3]Where dwell the gopīs, embodiments of divine love and rasa—Endless glory to the sacred land of Barsānā. [4]
author: Braj Rasik Heritage

title: Shri Radha Pad Pankaj Gahe Chhut Jaat Jag Dvand - Braj Ke Dohe
sanskrit_text: Shri Radha Pad Pankaj Gahe, Chhoot Jaat Jag-Dwand.Shri Radha Naam Adhaar Te, Vinashat Hain Yam-Phand.- Braj Ke DoheWhoever firmly holds the lotus feet of Shri Radha is released from all worldly sorrows and conflicts. One who performs bhajan of Shri Radha’s name destroys even the noose of Yamaraj (the god of death) and is taken directly to Her eternal abode.

One who performs bhajan of Shri Radha’s name destroys even the nuse of Yamaraj (the god of death) and is taken directly to Her eternal abode.

title: Vrindavan Vriksha Hain Ki Parijat - Shri Hare Krishnanand Sarasvati, Vrindavan Shatak (6)
sanskrit_text: (Kavitt)Vrindavan-Vriksha Hain Ki Paarijat Nandan Ke,Vrindavan-Shakha Ya Prem-Anjan-Shalaka Hain.Vrindavan-Raj Ya Rajat Renu-Raj Rahi,Vrindavan Path Hain Ki Prem-Puri-Naka Hain.Vrindavan-Kunj Ya Indra-Bhavan Shobhit Hain,Vrindavan-Dham Ya Niketan Prabha Ka Hain.Vrindavan-Phool Hain Ki Taravali Utari Ye,Vrindavan-Pat Hain Ki Prem Ki Pataka Hain.- Dandi Swami Shri Hare Krishnanand Sarasvati ‘Hare Krishn’, Vrindavan Shatak (6)Are these trees of Vṛndāvan or celestial Pārijāta trees in disguise?Are these branches, or wands touched with the collyrium of divine love? [1]Are these grains of Vṛndāvan’s dust, or shining pearls of purest silver scattered upon the earth?Are these pathways or the very gateways into the realm of divine love? [2]Are these bowers of Vṛndāvan, or dwellings resplendent beyond even Indra’s celestial palaces?Is this land just Vṛndāvan, or the very embodiment of beauty and divine radiance? [3]Are these flowers, or garlands of stars falling from the cosmos with divine fragrance?Are these Vṛndāvan’s leaves or fluttering flags of divine love? [4]

title: Gyan Karam Ru Upasana Sab Ahamiti Ko Mool - Shri Raskhan, Prem Vatika (12)
sanskrit_text: Gyan Karam Ru Upasana, Sab Ahamiti Ko Mool.Dridh Nischay Nahin Hot Bin, Kiye Prem Anukool.- Shri Raskhan, Prem Vatika (12)Knowledge, actions, and even devotional practices — all of these are rooted in ego. Unshakable faith in the Lord awakens only when one aligns oneself fully with the path of love (prema marga).
english_text: Gyan Karam Ru Upasana, Sab Ahamiti Ko Mul.Dridh Nischay Nahin Hot Bin, Kiye Prem Anukul.- Shri Raskhan, Prem Vatika (12)Knowledge, actions, and even devotional practices — all of these are ruted in ego. Unshakable faith in the Lord awakens only when one aligns oneself fully with the path of love (prema marga).
english_translation: Gyan Karam Ru Upasana, Sab Ahamiti Ko Mul.Dridh Nischay Nahin Hot Bin, Kiye Prem Anukul.- Shri Raskhan, Prem Vatika (12)Knowledge, actions, and even devotional practices — all of these are ruted in ego. Unshakable faith in the Lord awakens only when one aligns oneself fully with the path of love (prema marga).
author: Braj Rasik Heritage

title: Vrindavan Kyon Na Bhaye Ham Mor - Shri Parmanand Das, Parmanand Sagar (1375)
sanskrit_text: (Raag Malar)Vrindaavan Kyon Na Bhaye Ham Mor,Karat Nivaas Govardhan Upar, Nirakhat Nandkishor. [1]Kyon Na Bhaye Bansi Kul Sajani, Adhar Peebat Ghan Ghor.Kyon Na Bhaye Gunja Banaveli, Rahat Shyaam Ju Ki Or. [2]Kyon Na Bhaye Makaraakrit Kundal, Shyaam Shravan Jhakhajhor.Parmaanand Daas Ko Thaakur, Gopin Ke Chittachor. [3]- Shri Parmanand Das, Parmanand Sagar (1375)O creator! Why was I not born as a peacock in Vrindavan?There, I would dwell atop Govardhan, forever gazing at the enchanting son of Nanda, Shri Krishna. [1]O Sakhi, why was I not born as a flute resting upon Krishna’s lips, tasting His divine nectar? Why not a vine of wild gunja berries, always twining close to Shyam’s form? [2]Why not a makara-kundal (crocodile-shaped earring), adorning and gently swaying in Shri Shyamsundar’s ears?Says Paramananda Das—my beloved Thakur is none other than the thief of the gopis’ hearts, Lord Shri Krishna. [3]

title: Va Mukh Dekhan Ko Kaho - Shri Madhuri Das, Utkantha Madhuri (24)
sanskrit_text: Va Mukh Dekhan Ko Kaho, Keeje Kaun Upaay. Kaha Karaun Kaason Kahon, Pari Kathin Ati Aay.- Shri Madhuri Das, Utkantha Madhuri (24)What means shall I adopt so that I may behold the lotus faces of the Divine Couple, Shri Shyama-Shyam? What shall I do? Whom shall I turn to? This pain has now become utterly unbearable.

title: Moson Nahin Kachhuk Baniaayi - Shri Lalit Kishori, Abhilash Madhuri, Vinay (73)
sanskrit_text: (Raag Malkaus)Moson Nahin Kachhuk Baniaayi.Hon Sadaiv Augunki Bhaajan, Kooti Kooti Kari Bhari Burayi. [1]Haha Kripakaraun Swamini Ab, Tuv Padapankaj Mein Shir Nayi.Lalitkishori Braj Darasavo, Dekho Nijagun Maana Badhayi. [2]- Shri Lalit Kishori, Abhilash Madhuri, Vinay (73)O Shri Radha! Nothing I do ever turns out right. I have always been full of faults — wickedness is deeply rooted within me. [1]O Swamini! Alas, please have mercy on me now—I bow my head at Your lotus feet. Shri Lalit Kishori humbly prays — “O supremely compassionate Kishori Ji! Please glance upon your causeless merciful nature, and bless this destitute soul with the darshan of your holy land of Braj.” [2]

title: Aay Sakat Nahin Gira Mein Sampradaay Mam Reet - Shri Charan Das
sanskrit_text: Aay Sakat Nahin Gira Mein, Sampradaay Mam Reet.Prem Sampradaay Naam Hai, Kathyo Kachhuk Lakhai Preet.- Shri Charan DasThe nature of my tradition cannot be described through mere words. It is called the Path of Love (Prem Sampraday), and even a slight experience or expression of it is possible only through love itself.
english_text: Aay Sakat Nahin Gira Mein, Sampraday Mam Rit.Prem Sampraday Nam Hai, Kathyo Kachhuk Lakhai Prit.- Shri Charan DasThe nature of my tradition cannot be described through mere words. title: Hari Ji Baanh Gaho Ab Meri - Shri Guru Chhauna Ji Maharaj
sanskrit_text: Hari Ji Baanh Gaho Ab Meri, Bhav Saagar Son Kaadho.Ya Jag Mein Koi Hitoo Na Mera, Phand Paryau Hai Gaadho. [1]Paancho Chor Base Ghat Bheetar, Mamat Daari Faansi.‘Guruchhauna’ Ko Apna Karkai, Raakho Charann Paasi. [2]- Shri Guruchauna Ji Maharaj, Vinah Ki MaanjhHari Ji, please now take hold of my arm and lift me out of this ocean of material existence.In this world, I have no true well-wisher, instead, I am trapped in a web of worldly entanglements. [1]The five thieves (lust, anger, greed, attachment, and ego) have taken residence within my heart, and attachment has placed a noose around my neck.Please accept me as your own, O Lord Krishn, and keep me near your lotus feet (i.e., Sri Vrindavan) — this is the humble plea of your servant, Sri Guruchhauna. [2]

[2]

title: Pankaj Vishdhar Meen Mrig - Shri Narayan Swami, Braj Vihar, Maan Leela Dohavali (94)
sanskrit_text: Pankaj Vishdhar Meen Mrig, Sar Khanjan Baadaam.Pyaari Tere Drigan Ke, Yah Bin Daam Gulaam.- Shri Narayan Swami, Braj Vihar, Maan Leela Dohavali (94)O Pyari Ju (Shri Radha)! The lotus, serpent, fish, deer, arrow, wagtail bird, and even almonds—all have become sold servants to Your eyes without any price, for the enchanting beauty of Your eyes leaves their charms meaningless.
english_text: Pankaj Vishdhar Min Mrig, Sar Khanjan Badam.Pyari Tere Drigan Ke, Yah Bin Dam Gulam.- Shri Narayan Swami, Braj Vihar, Man Lila Dohavali (94)O Pyari Ju (Shri Radha)! The lotus, serpent, fish, dir, arrow, wagtail bird, and even almonds—all have become sold servants to Your eyes without any price, for the enchanting beauty of Your eyes leaves their charms meaningless.

title: पोढे हरि राधिका के भवन - श्री कुंभनदास, श्री कुम्भनदास जी की वाणी
sanskrit_text:
(राग केदार)
पोढे हरि राधिका के भवन। [1]
बिजना व्यार करत ललितादिक शीतल आवत पवन॥ [2]
सुन कें कान शीतल भई छतियाँ विरह दु:ख के दवन। [3]
दास कुम्भन धर्यो ललिता नाम राधा रवन (रमण)॥ [4]
- श्री कुंभनदास, श्री कुम्भनदास जी की वाणी
english_text: (rag kedara) podhe hari radhika ke bhavan. [1] bijana vyar karat lalitadik shital avat pavan.. [2] sun ken kan shital bhai chhatiyan virah du:kh ke davan. [3] das kumbhan dharyo lalita nam radha ravan (ramana).. [4] - shri kunbhanadas, shri kumbhanadas ji ki vani

title: अहु राधे वृषभानु की - श्री भट्ट देवाचार्य, युगल शतक (81)
sanskrit_text:
अहु राधे वृषभानु की, कुँवरी किसोरी बाल।
थोरी बै भौरीहि में, मोहे मोहन लाल॥
- श्री भट्ट देवाचार्य, युगल शतक (81)
english_text: ahu radhe vrishabhanu ki, kunvari kisori bal. thori bai bhaurihi men, mohe mohan lal.. - shri bhatt devachary, yugal shatak (81)

title: हौं बलिहारी भक्तकी - श्री हरिराम व्यास, व्यास वाणी, साखी (64)
sanskrit_text:
हौं बलिहारी भक्तकी, कर्यौ बहुत उपकार।
हरि सो धन हिरदै धर्यौ, छुटा दियौ संसार॥
- श्री हरिराम व्यास, व्यास वाणी, साखी (64)
english_text: haun balihari bhaktaki, karyau bahut upakar. hari so dhan hiradai dharyau, chhuta diyau snsar.. - shri hariram vyas, vyas vani, sakhi (64)

title: कुसुम सेज पिय प्यारी पौढे करत है रस बतियाँ - श्री हरिराय जी
sanskrit_text:
(राग केदारो)
कुसुम सेज पिय प्यारी पौढे करत है रस बतियाँ। [1]
हँसत परस्पर आनंद हुलसत लटक लटक लपटात छतियाँ॥ [2]
अतिरस रंगभीने रीझे री रिझवार
एक तनमन भई एकमति गतियाँ। [3]
रसिक सुजान निर्भय क्रीड़त दोऊ
अंग अंग प्रति विंबित दोऊन के बसन भतियाँ॥ [4]
- श्री हरिराय जी
english_text: (rag kedaro) kusum sej piy pyari paudhe karat hai ras batiyan. [1] hnsat paraspar annd hulasat latak latak lapatat chhatiyan.. [2] atiras rngabhine rijhe ri rijhavar ek tanaman bhai ekamati gatiyan. [3] rasik sujan nirbhay kridat duo ang ang prati vinbit duon ke basan bhatiyan.. [4] - shri hariray ji
english_translation: (rag kedaro) kusum sej piy pyari paudhe karat hai ras batiyan. [1] hnsat paraspar annd hulasat latak latak lapatat chhatiyan.. [2] atiras rngabhine rijhe ri rijhavar ek tanaman bhai ekamati gatiyan. [3] rasik sujan nirbhay kridat duo ang ang prati vinbit duon ke basan bhatiyan.. [4] - shri hariray ji

title: Shri Vrishabhan Se Rane Jahaan - Shri Kishori Ali
sanskrit_text: (Sawaiya)Shri Vrishabhan Se Raane Jahaan,Raani Kirati Ki Jahan Keerati Chaaje. [1]Mohan Hu Bikasaane Rahain,Ju Sihaane ‘Kishori Ali’ Bane Raajain. [2]Heeye Sadaa Harashaane Rahain,Sarasaane Rahain Pag Sevan Kaajain. [3]Ko Barasane Ki Rees Karai,Jaake Sees Pai Radhika Raani Viraajain. [4]- Shri Kishori AliThe place where a King like Śrī Vṛṣabhanu reigns, and where Queen Kīrti’s fame spreads gloriously in every direction. [1]Where even Śrī Kṛṣṇa remains ever delighted, for Kiśorī Jī (Śrī Rādhā) reigns on the royal throne, and even He is under Her loving sway. [2]Where His heart remains ever joyful, immersed in the sweet service of Śrī Rādhāraṇī’s lotus feet. title: Radha Pati Gati Ek Tum Mokao Aur Na Thaun - Shri Vrindavan Das Chacha Ji, Vivek Lakshan Beli (107)
sanskrit_text: Radha Pati Gati Ek Tum, Mokaun Aur Na Thaun.‘Vrindaavan Hit’ Raavari, Tahal Dehu Bali Jaun.- Shri Vrindavan Das Chacha Ji, Vivek Lakshan Beli (107)O beloved of Radha (Shri Krishna)! You are my one and only refuge—there is no other shelter for me. title: Deh Dhare Ko Ab Phal Paayo - Shri Nagridas Ji (Maharaj Sawant Singh) Ki Vani, Chootak Pad (121)
sanskrit_text: Deh Dhare Ko Ab Phal Paayo.Beete Bahut Divas Asamajhas, Maya Naach Nachaayo.Thoharban Tai Mohi Kaadhi Thir, Vrindaavipun Basaayo.Kaun Kripa Anayaas Bhaee Haun, Nij Man Heri Hiraayo.Nisadin Pahar Ghari Chin Chin Pal, Nit Anand Rahai Sarasayo.Nagaridas Daas Hvai Kai Jo, Yahaan Na Aayo So Pachhitaayo.- Shri Nagridas Ji (Maharaj Sawant Singh), Shri Nagridas Ji Ki Vani, Chootak Pad (121)At last, the true purpose of this human life has been fulfilled. For so long, Maya led me astray, making me dance helplessly to her illusion. [1]But by the causeless grace of the Lord, I was rescued from that barren forest of worldly existence and brought to rest in the divine land of Sri Dham Vrindavan. What sudden mercy has descended! As I look within, my heart is filled with wonder. [2]Day and night, every moment overflows with an unending stream of bliss. Shri Nagari Das warns: Whoever is a servant of the Lord, yet fails to take shelter in Vrindavan, will one day weep with regret. [3]

title: Shri Biharidas Man Son Kahai - Shri Biharin Dev Ji Ki Vani, Siddhant Ki Saakhi (265)
sanskrit_text: Shri Biharidas Man Soun Kahai, Ab Na Lagaun Tohi.Jas Gaaun Haridas Kau, Tain Sukh Deenon Mohi.- Shri Biharin Dev Ji, Shri Biharin Dev Ji Ki Vani, Siddhant Ki Saakhi (265)Shri Biharindev instructs his mind—“Now, completely isolate yourself from all directions and firmly fix yourself in the rasa-glory of Swami Shri Haridas, for the bliss found in the uninterrupted, eternal Akhand Nitya-Vihar rasa of the Divine Couple (Shri Shyama Kunjbihari) is not found anywhere else.”

title: Shri Harivansh Sarana Je Aye - Sri Neh Nagridas Ji Ki Vani, Siddhant (136)
sanskrit_text: (Raga Gauri)Shri Harivansha Sarana Je Aye. Shri Vrishabhanukumari Namdanandana, Nijakara Apani Chitthi Chadhaaye. [1]Diye Mukaraya Kachu Nahi Goyau, Kiye Manoratha Mana Ke Bhaye. Shrivyasa Suvana Charanana Raja Parasata, ‘Nagaridasa’ Se Ranka Jivaye. [2]- Shri Neh Nagridas, Sri Neh Nagridas Ji Ki Vani, Siddhant (136)Whoever sought the shelter of Shri Harivansh Mahaprabhu Ji, their name was personally written by the Divine Couple, Shri Radha-Krishna, in the register of their own devotees. [1]They unveiled every divine secret to him, concealing nothing, and fulfilling their every desire. Shri Nagaridas Ji says, “Even a fallen soul like me was revived with new life. I bow and place the dust of Vyasji's son Shri Harivansh Mahaprabhu Ji’s lotus feet upon my head.” [2]

title: Piya Piyari Seja Banai Aaj -  Shri Lalitmohini Dev, Ras Ke Pad (47)
sanskrit_text: Piya Piyari Seja Banai Aaj.Piyari Jhalaka, Chamaka Saba Piyare, Piyare Basana Bane Saba Kaja. [1] Piyare Phula Bane Saba Tana Mem, Piyari Sobha Sahaja Samaja. Shrilalitamohini Yaha Sukha Dekhata, Syama Tanaim Piyare Saba Saja. [2]- Shri Lalit Mohini Dev, Lalit Mohini Dev Ju Ki Vaani, Ras Ke Pad (47)Today, the Beloved has decorated a yellow bed; everything around glows with golden-yellow brilliance. He has also adorned His body with yellow garments. [1]His entire form is decorated with yellow-colored flowers made of sandalwood, saffron, and other fragrant substances. Gazing upon each limb of Shri Shyamasundar, adorned with the golden radiance of Shri Radha, whose natural hue is golden-yellow, is my soul’s greatest bliss, says Lalitmohini. [2]

title: Kouka Anga Bibhuti Lagavata - Shri Sundar Ji
sanskrit_text: (Savaiya)Kouka Amga Bibhuti Lagavata, Kouka Hota Nirata Digambara. [1]Kouka Sveta Kashaika Audhata, Kouka Katha Ramgai Bahu Ambara. [2]Kouka Balkala Shisha Jata Nakha, Kouka Audhata Haim Ju Baghambara. [3]Sundara Eka Aj~nana Gaye Binu, Ye Saba Disata Ahi Adambara. [4]- Shri Sundardas JiSome smear ashes on their bodies, some go completely naked as digambaras. [1]Some wear white ascetic robes, some dye garments made of wood fiber in various colors. [2]Some keep matted hair atop their heads, wear bark garments, and grow long nails. Some dress in tiger skins to appear fierce and detached. [3]Sundar Jī says—without true knowledge of the Supreme and sincere devotion in the heart, all these outward practices are nothing but pretense and show. [4]

title: Pati Ke Panv Palothahin Sindhu-Sutaa Gunvant -  Braj Ke Dohe
sanskrit_text: Pati Ke Pany Palothahin, Sindhu-Sutaa Gunvant.Bhaanusutaa Pad Paras Kau, Avasar Taakat Kant.- Braj Ke DoheThe daughter of the ocean, Goddess Lakshmi, an embodiment of virtues, eternally serves her Husband, Lord Shri Hari, by gently pressing His feet. The very same Shri Hari, however, seeks the opportunity to serve the lotus feet of His Swamini (governess), the one and only—Shri Radha.

The very same Shri Hari, however, siks the opportunity to serve the lotus fit of His Swamini (governess), the one and only—Shri Radha.

title: Maai Moko Jugalnaam Nidhi Bhaai - Shri Yugal Priya
sanskrit_text: (Raag Ramkali, Taal Titāla)Maai Moko Jugalnaam Nidhi Bhaai.Sukh-Sampada Jagat Ki Jhoothi, Aai Sang Na Jaai. [1]Lobhi Ko Dhan Kaam Na Aavai, Antakaal Dukhdaai.Jo Jorai Dhan Adham Karam Ten, Sarbas Chhalai Nasāi. [2]Kul Ke Dharam Kahaa Lai Keejai, Bhakti Na Man Mein Aai.‘Jugalpriya’ Sab Tajau Bhajau Hari, Charan Kamal Man Laai. [3]- Shri Yugal PriyaO friend! My heart has found its true treasure in the divine names of the Divine Couple. All the pleasures and riches of this world are false—they do not accompany the soul at the time of death. [1]Even a miser’s wealth cannot help him; instead, it becomes a source of suffering in the end. Wealth earned through impure means ultimately leads to the ruin of the future. [2]What is the value of social position, family reputation, or religious practices if love for the Lord does not grow? Shri Yugal Priya says: The true purpose of life lies in surrendering the mind at the lotus feet of Shri Hari through pure, selfless devotion. [3]

title: Ab Rahihaun Brajbhumi Ki Hvai Pagmarag Dhuri -  Nanddas Granthwali, Bhanwar Geet (66.2)
sanskrit_text: Ab Rahihaun Brajbhoomi Ki, Hvai Pagmarag Dhuri.Vicharat Pad Mopai Parai, Sab Sukh Jeevan Muri.- Shri Nanddas, Nanddas Granthwali, Bhanwar Geet (66.2)The self-realized Uddhava says—“O Lord! My only wish now is to forever reside in Braj, becoming one with the dust of this sacred land, so that when the maidens of Braj, the pinnacle of divine love, wander through these sacred paths, may the dust of their feet fall upon me. In that moment, I shall feel truly fulfilled. This alone is the supreme purpose of my life.”

title: Sada Sakhi Sun Vraj Hi Mein Rahno - Shri Dwarkesh Ji
sanskrit_text: (Raag Vihag)Sada Sakhi Sun Vraj Hi Mein Rahno.Man Ki Vyatha Kunjkunjan Mein, Lata Pataa Prati Kahnno. [1]Oran Son Kahaa Kaaj Hamen Ab, Aan Pare So Sahnno.Yugal Kishor Keli Ras Sangam, Smaran Karat Man Dahnno. [2]Rasikan Sang Hilmil Priya Sajani, Kachhukh Goodh Ras Gahnno.‘Dwarkesh’ Antar Ras Sangam, Ubhay Udadhi Mein Bahanno. [3]- Shri Dwarkesh JiListen, O friend, let us always dwell in Vraj alone. There, I will express the pain of my heart to each vine and leaf within the forest bowers. [1]I have no concern with others now—whatever comes, I will quietly endure. As I remember the divine love-play of the youthful couple, my heart yearns with longing. [2]In the company of rasik devotees, I will grasp some very hidden rasa there. title: Pranavau Barsano Sukhadham - Shri Radha Priya (Radhikanath)
sanskrit_text: Pranavau Barsano Sukhadham.Jahaan Virajat Mohan Shyama, Keerti Bhaanu Lali Shridham. [1]Vidhi-Giri, Peeri, Bhanusar, Gahvar, Morakuti Abhiram.Daan, Vilaas, Maangarh-Leela, Saankari Khor Lalam. [2]Surat Samarsar Lalit Bihaarahin, Drumballi Vrat Tham.Radha-Priya Nit Sevat Douu, Shatritau Aathon Yam. [3]- Shriradha Priya Ji [Radhikanath Ji]I bow down to Barsana, the abode of divine bliss, where Sri Krishn and Sri Radha, along with Kirtiji, Sri Vrishbhanu, and Shridama, lovingly reside. [1]Places like Brahma Parvat (where Brahma Ji resides in the form of a mountain), Peeri Pokhar, Bhanusarovar, Gahvarvan, and Morakuti are deeply charming. This sacred land is home to divine pastimes such as Daangarh (the tax pastime), Vilaasgarh (joyful play), the renowned Maangarh (Radha’s sulking pastimes), and Sankari Khor (the narrow, sacred lane), where many of Radha-Krishna’s divine leelas unfold. [2]In this holy land, surata-samar (love-filled divine battles) and Lalita-bihār (love-plays of the divine couple) continually take place amidst enchanting groves and blossoming creepers. Here, the six seasons serve the divine couple, day and night, says Shri Radya Priya Ji. [3]

title: Naam Roop Leela Lalit Aur Jaaniye Dham - Sri Saras Madhuri
sanskrit_text: Naam Roop Leela Lalit, Aur Jaaniye Dham.Inki Sudridh Upaasana, Karai Rasik Nishkaam.- Shri Saras MadhuriThose who engage in firm and exclusive devotion to the name, form, beautiful leelas, and abode of the divine couple, Shri Radha Krishna, are known as Rasikas. The most essential aspect of their devotion is that it is completely selfless (nishkaam) and ‘tatsukhmayi’—meaning, their sole aim is to give happiness to the divine couple, not to seek personal happiness or liberation.

title: E Dou Rajata Ramga Bhare Ri - Shri Albeli Ali, Samay Prabandh (166)
sanskrit_text: (Raga Purabi)E Dou Rajata Ramga Bhare Ri. Bhuja Jorem Samvala Tana Gorem, Gahi Druma Dari Khare Ri. [1] Pulakata Amga Anamga Chake Chavi, Batana Ranga Dhere Ri. Pana Bhare Mukha Sukha Sarasane, Arujhane Drriga Pala Visare Ri. [2] Navala Chaila Chitavata Pritama Tana, Hansi Hansi Prana Hare Ri. Alabeli Ali Rupa Taramgani, Naina Mina Pare Ri. [3]- Shri Albeli Ali, Samay Prabandh (166)The duo, fair-complexioned Shri Radha and dark-complexioned Shri Krishna, stand resplendent in hues of divine love, with arms around each other’s necks, holding onto a tree branch. [1]Their bodies are thrilled, completely intoxicated in divine love’s ecstasy; every word exchanged between them is drenched in the colors of love. Their mouths, filled with red betel leaves, overflow with sweetness; their eyes remain lovingly fixed on one another, forgetting even to blink. [2]The ever-fresh and most charming Shri Radha gazes at her beloved, and with enchanting smiles, steals away His very life-breath. Albeli Aliji is swaying in the waves of beauty showered by the divine couple, her eyes caught like a fish in their divine glances. [3]

title: Houn Rusongi Kunwari Son Kunwari Manave Mohi - Shri Vanshi Ali, Hriday Sarvasv (39)
sanskrit_text: Houn Rusongi Kunwari Son, Kunwari Manavai Mohi.Kunwari Jo Mo Saun Rusi Hai, Hon Paayini Paron Nihohi.- Shri Vanshi Ali, Hriday Sarvasv (39)If ever I sulk in love with ever-youthful Shri Radha, She is the one who sweetly consoles me. But if She ever turns away in sulking love, I would fall at Her lotus feet, doing all I can to pacify and bring back Her smile.

title: Pyari Ladili Padaravind Nain - Shri Harivyas Devacharya, Mahavani, Sahaj Sukh (93)

[1]Koti Jatan Karahu Kou Phirat Naahi Phere.Shriharipriya Sahaj Subhaav Gahi Rahe Anere. [2]- Shri Harivyas Devacharya, Mahavani, Sahaj Sukh (93)(Doha)Shri Krishna says, “O Radhe! My eyes, like enchanted bees, are so intoxicated by the nectar of love at Your lotus feet that they hover around them without pause, day and night.”(Pada)O beloved Ladiliju! Not only do they draw near, but even from afar, my eye-like bumblebees remain firmly fixed upon the lotus feet of my dearest Priyaju (Sri Radha). [2]

title: Shri Radha Ko Vrindavan Rasamay - Shri Hita Vrindavan Das
sanskrit_text: (Shri) Radha Ko Vrindavan Rasamay, Mohan Ko Pyaro Lagai Ati Hai. [1]Paind Ek Kari Tajat Na Seenwa, Pritam Ki Aisi Bhai Gati Hai. [2]Yaaten Gahyo Ananyani Dhrid Kari, Man Kram Bach Badi Nirmal Rati Hai. [3]‘Vrindavan Hit’ Roop Dham Yah Jahan Badhati Dampati Sampati Hai. [4]- Chacha Hita Vrindavan DasShri Radha’s Vrindavan is filled with supremely divine nectar and is exceedingly dear to the enchanter, Shri Krishna. [1]So deep is Shri Krishna’s love towards Vrindavan that He does not place even a single step beyond its boundaries. [2]For this reason, the rasik devotees maintain an unwavering commitment to Vrindavan with their mind, actions, and speech. Their pure love continues to increase day by day. [3]Chacha Vrindavan Das says, This Vrindavan is the abode of pure love, where, simply by residing without offense, the divine wealth of the divine couple (Shri Radha-Krishna) keeps expanding endlessly. [4]

title: Rahay Ang Sang Anang Harain Manu - Shri Biharin Dev Ji Ki Vani, Ras Ke Sewaiya (30)
sanskrit_text: (Sawaiya)Rahay Ang Sang Anang Harain Manu Neerad Neel Daamini Damkain. [1]Barni Na Parai Chhavi Kou Kavi Tai Sat Sesh Mahesh Ki Buddhi Samkain. [2]Shri Bihaari-Biharini Daasi Nikunjan Nirkhat Hi Sukh Prem Ramkain. [3]Chitai Var Raaj Biharini Nitt Adbhut Jyoti Chibuk Chamakain. [4]- Shri Biharin Dev Ji, Shri Biharin Dev Ji Ki Vani, Ras Ke Sewaiya (30)They remain constantly together, their beauty stealing the heart of Kāmadeva (Cupid). Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s form is like a fresh raincloud, while Śrī Rādhā shines like a brilliant lightning streak. [1]No poet or sage, not even those blessed with the highest intellect—like Śeṣanāga with his hundred mouths or Maheśa (Lord Śiva)—can fully describe their enchanting beauty. [2]Śrī Bihārin Dās, the servant of Bihārī-Bihāriṇī, revels in divine love-bliss, beholding Their love-plays in the ever-fresh bowers (nikunjas). [3]Vihāriṇī Rānī, Śrī Rādhā, reigns forever over my heart, whose divine radiance shines most wondrously. [4]

english_translation: (Sawaiya)Rahay Ang Sang Anang Harain Manu Nirad Nil Damini Damkain. [1]Barni Na Parai Chhavi Kou Kavi Tai Sat Sesh Mahesh Ki Buddhi Samkain. [2]Shri Bihari-Biharini Dasi Nikunjan Nirkhat Hi Sukh Prem Ramkain. [3]Chitai Var Raj Biharini Nitt Adbhut Jyoti Chibuk Chamakain. [4]- Shri Biharin Dev Ji, Shri Biharin Dev Ji Ki Vani, Ras Ke Sewaiya (30)They remain constantly together, their beauty stealing the heart of Kāmadeva (Cupid). Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s form is like a fresh raincloud, while Śrī Rādhā shines like a brilliant lightning streak. [1]No poet or sage, not even those blessed with the highest intellect—like Śeṣanāga with his hundred mouths or Maheśa (Lord Śiva)—can fully describe their enchanting beauty. [2]Śrī Bihārin Dās, the servant of Bihārī-Bihāriṇī, revels in divine love-bliss, beholding Their love-plays in the ever-fresh bowers (nikunjas). [3]Vihāriṇī Rānī, Śrī Rādhā, reigns forever over my heart, whose divine radiance shines most wondrously. [4]
author: Braj Rasik Heritage

title: Ek Akhandit Ekras Niravadhi Rati Jo Hoi - Shri Rasik Dev Ju Ki Vani, Vishistha Pada & Saakhi (4)
sanskrit_text: Ek Akhandit Ekras, Niravadhi Rati Jo Hoi.Milat Milat Virah Na Ghatai, Prem Kahat Hain Soi.- Shri Rasik Dev, Shri Rasik Dev Ju Ki Vani, Vishistha Pada & Saakhi (4)That love which is uninterrupted, unwavering, and endless, where even in union, the longing does not diminish but continually increases, that alone is called pure love.

title: Jai Jai Jai Nandju Ke Nandan - Braj Ke Kavitt
sanskrit_text: (Kavitt)Jai Jai Jai Nandju Ke Nandan Naval Laal,Jai Jai Jai Shri Radheju Bhaanu Ki Dulaari Ki. [1]Jai Jai Jasodaju Ke Baare Brajchandju Ki,Jai Jai Hamaari Pyaari Keerti Kumari Ki. [2]Gokul Jubaraaj Gokules-Kulsekhar Ki,Shrivan Ki Rani Radhe Barsaanewari Ki. [3]Gopijan Vallabh Govind Shri Shyama-Shyaam,Bolo Sab Mili Radha Vallabh Bihari Ki. [4]- Braj Ke Kavitt Glory, glory to the ever‑youthful son of Nanda Mahārāj!Glory, glory to Śrī Rādhā, the beloved daughter of King Vṛṣabhānu. [1]Glory to the darling son of Yashodā, the moon of Braj,Glory to our beloved Pyārījū, the charming daughter of Kīrtijī. [2]Glory to the prince of Gokul, the Lord of Gokul, the crown jewel of His dynasty — Śrī Kṛṣṇa!Glory to Rādhā, the queen of Vṛndāvan and the darling of Barsaṇā. [3]Glory to the beloved of the cowherds, Govinda,Glory to Śrī Śyāma‑Śyām! Let us all proclaim victory to the divine couple, Śrī Rādhā Vallabh Bihārī! [4]

title: Sa Nasti Trishu Lokeshu Yasya - Bhavishya Purana
sanskrit_text: Sa Nasti Trishu Lokeshu Yasya Tisthamyahm Vashe.Vina Radham Priytamam Pranebyopi Gareeyseem.- Bhavishya PuranaLord Krishn says to Narada, “No one in all three worlds has control over me except Sri Radha, my beloved, who is dearer to me than my own life.”

title: Jab Jab Murli Kaanh Bajavat - Shri Surdas, Sura Sagara
sanskrit_text: Jab Jab Murli Kaanh Bajaavat,Tab-Tab Radha Naam Uchaaraat, Baarambaar Rijhaavat. [1]Tum Ramani Vah Raman Tumhaare, Vaisehin Mohin Janaavat.Murli Bhai Sauti Jo Maai, Teri Tahal Karaavat. [2]Vah Daasi Tum Hari-Ardhangini, Yah Merai Man Aavat.Soor Pragat Tahi Soun Kahi-Kahi, Tumkau Shyaam Bulaavat. [3]- Shri Surdas, Sura SagaraSaint Surdas, adopting the mood of a sakhī (female companion), speaks to Shri Radha:Whenever Shri Krishna plays His flute, again and again He utters the name “Radha,” trying to please You. [1]You, Radha, are the beloved, and He is your devoted lover. He always conveys to me that He belongs entirely to you. The flute has become like your co-wife, yet she only serves you. [2]A thought arises in my mind — the flute is Your maidservant, and You are Hari’s ardhāṃgini (the very half of Hari’s being). Surdas says, “Again and again, O Radhe! Shyamasundar is calling out to you through that flute.” [3]

[2]Vah Dasi Tum Hari-Ardhangini, Yah Merai Man Aavat.Sur Pragat Tahi Soun Kahi-Kahi, Tumkau Shyam Bulavat. title: Pritam Mera Ek Tu Sundar Aur Na Koi - Shri Sundar Ji
sanskrit_text: Preetam Mera Ek Tu, ‘Sundar’ Aur Na Koi.Gupt Bhaya Kis Kaaraaj, Kaahi Na Pargat Hoi.- Shri Sundar JiO, my dearest Lord! You alone are my beloved. For what reason are you hidden from me? Why do you not now reveal Yourself and grant me Your vision?

title: Jugalvar Jaanat Ho Sab Baat - Shri Roop Madhuri Ji Ki Vani, Padavali (100)
sanskrit_text: (Raag Todi)Jugalvar Jaanat Ho Sab Baat.Vrindaavan Mein Vaas Dehum Mohe, Aur Kachu Nahin Bhat. [1]Braj Raj Mein Lotun Nit Prati Main, Ab To Yahi Suhaat.Naam Ratun Tumaro Nishi Baasar, Yahi Sadaa Man Aat. [2]Darshan Kar Tumare Daasan Ke, Hiy Aanand Sarasaat.‘Roopmaadhuri’ Kripa Karo Ab, Ye Din Beete Jaat. [3]- Shri Roop Madhuri, Shri Roop Madhuri Ji Ki Vani, Padavali (100)O Divine Couple, You know everything. Please grant me residence in Vrindavan, for nothing else pleases my heart. [1]There, I shall roll in the dust of Braj each day—this alone brings me joy. I will chant Your names day and night; this is the constant desire of my heart. [2]I shall behold the darshan of Your devotees, which will fill my heart with bliss. Roopmadhuri says, “Please shower Your mercy, for the precious days of my life are slipping away without Vrindavan.” [3]

title: Vyas Radhika Ravan Binu - Shri Hariram Vyas, Vyas Vani, Siddhant Ki Saakhi (31)
sanskrit_text: Vyas Radhika-Ravan Binu, Kahun Na Paayau Sukh.Daarani-Daarani Main Phiryau, Paatani-Paatani Dukh.- Shri Hariram Vyas, Vyas Vani, Siddhant Ki Saakhi (31)Without my divine couple, Sri Radhika Raman, who are the source of all, says Hariram Vyas, I have found no joy anywhere. Wandering from branch to branch, I have become entangled, and every leaf brings nothing but sorrow.

title: Mo Nirdhan Ki Lalita Sampati - Shri Vanshi Ali, Siddhant Ke Pad (34)
sanskrit_text: Mo Nirdhan Ki Lalita Sampati.Chhin Na Sakat Bisraay Jeey Te, Mohi Lataki Laagat Pal Jhampati. [1]Jaay Nirkhi Pyari Gad-Gad Hwai, Ank Lagani Pulakit Tan Kampati.Jai Shri Vanshi Ali Shri Radha Bali Nit Prati Chaahat Nit Charanan Ko Champati. [2]- Shri Vanshi Ali, Siddhant Ke Pad (34)Lalita Sakhi is the sole treasure of this destitute soul (me). My heart cannot forget Her even for a moment, for it remains bound to Her, swaying with Her every moment. [1]Whenever Lalitaji beholds Pyariju (Sri Radha), waves of ecstasy arise within Her, and when Radha embraces Her, Her limbs tremble with divine love-bliss. Shri Vanshi Ali says, “Lalita Ji endlessly sacrifices Herself for Sri Radha, ever yearning to serve Her lotus feet lovingly.” [2]

title: Vrindaban Raajain Duvau Saajai Sukh Ke Saaj - Braj Ke Dohe
sanskrit_text: Vrindaban Raajain Duvau, Saajai Sukh Ke Saaj.Maharani Radha Utai, Maharaj Brajraj.- Braj Ke DoheIn Vrindavan, divine arrangements for bliss are beautifully adorned, where the ever youthful divine couple shines in full splendor. On one side, Lord Shri Krishna is enthroned; on the other, the Queen of Vrindavan, Shri Radhika, adorns the scene with her matchless radiance.

title: Chhabili Radhe Kab Darasan Daiho - Braj Nidhi Granthawali, Braj Nidhi Pad Sangrah (25)
sanskrit_text: (Raag Dhanashri)Chhabeeli Radhe Kab Darasan Daihau.Tuv-Mukh-Chand-Chakori Ankhiyani, Roop-Sudha Achvaihau. [1]Yah Aasa Laagi Rahai Nis-Din, Kab Man Tapat Bujhaihau.Karikai Kripa Kahau “Brajanidhi” Ko, Kab Apanau Kari Laihau. [2]- Shri Braj Nidhi Ji, Braj Nidhi Granthawali, Braj Nidhi Pad Sangrah (25)O Charming Radha, when will you grant me Your darshan? Like the chakori bird thirsting for the moon, my eyes long for the nectar of Your form. [1]Only the hope of beholding You sustains me day and night—when will the burning in my heart be soothed? Sri Braj Nidhi says, “When will You bless me by accepting me as Your own? Please answer, O treasure of Braj, Sri Radhey!” [2]

title: Praan Ik Dvai Khinhe Bhakti-Preeti-Prakaas - Shri Surdas, Sura Sagara
sanskrit_text: Praan Ik Dvai Khinhe, Bhakti-Preeti-Prakaas!Soor Swaami Swaamini Mili, Karat Rang-Vilaas.- Shri Surdas, Sura SagaraTheir soul is one, but they have assumed two forms only to spread and illuminate devotion and love. title: Jinke Deh Neh Ras Bhine - Shri Hita Roop Lal
sanskrit_text: Jinke Deh Neh Ras Bheene,Tinke Nayan Prem Madmaate, Naate Jag Ke Neku Na Cheene. [1]Ved Bhed Taji Nem Shrinkhala, Vihansi Bhaye Priyatam Soun Leene.Jai Shri Roopalal Hit Gati Mati Nyaari, Kahi Na Jaat Jaise Jal Meene. [2]- Shri Hita Roop LalThose rare, most fortunate souls who are drenched in the nectar of divine love (prema-rasa) of God, their eyes remain intoxicated with love. Under the influence of that divine love, they lose all awareness of worldly relationships. [1]They joyfully cast off the shackles of Vedas, scriptures, and social conventions, absorbed entirely in loving devotion. Shri Hit Rupalal Ji says: such rasika lovers attain a state of consciousness so unique and unfathomable that words fail to capture it. Their union with the beloved Lord is like that of a fish with water—inseparable. [2]

[1]They joyfully cast off the shackles of Vedas, scriptures, and social conventions, absorbed entirely in loving devotion. Shri Hit Rupalal Ji says: such rasika lovers attain a state of consciousness so unique and unfathomable that words fail to capture it. Their union with the beloved Lord is like that of a fish with water—inseparable. [2]
author: Braj Rasik Heritage

title: Aaj Kaal Kalp Jo Pai Baraah Barat Rahyo - Shri Chhabile Vallabh Goswami
sanskrit_text: (Kavitt)Aaj Kaal Kalp Jo Pai Baaraah Barat Rahyo,Jaake Or Chor Aadi Hi Son Je Paran Hain. [1]Jaa Hi Kaaranai Jaako Naam Akhatij Paryo,Aksh Hot Tushy Savai Ya Son Karan Hain. [2]Aaj Din Jhaanki Jo Nihaare Shri Bihari Ju Ki,Aap Hi Yamraaj Taaki Let Ye Sharan Hain. [3]Sevai Haridaas Roop Raashi Mein ‘Chhabeelay’ Ramy,Bhakt Man Bhaavate Bihari Ke Charan Hain. [4]- Shri Chhabile Vallabh GoswamiToday, on Akshaya Tritiya, unfolds a Kalpa‑worthy day whose fruit endures through eternity, whose beginning and end are connected to the eternal. [1]This is why it is called ‘Akhatīja’ — for all auspicious deeds performed today become inexhaustible and yield eternal blessings. [2]Whoever beholds the divine form (Jhānki) of Śrī Bihārījī today — even Yamarāj (the god of death), who seeks His lotus feet, does them no harm. [3]The lotus feet of Bihārījī, an ocean of nectarean beauty, lovingly served by Svāmī Haridās, forever delight the hearts of rasik devotees, says Śrī Chhabīle Vallabh Goswāmījī. [4]

Sahjobai says—the world may call them mad, but they have transcended the boundaries of society and scripture.

title: Bhajan Bin Hai Chola Bekam - Sri Roop Kunwari Ji
sanskrit_text: (Raag Peelu - Taal Titala)Bhajan Bin Hai Chola Bekam.Mal Aru Mutra Bharo Nar Sab Tan, Hai Nishfal Yah Cham. [1]Bin Hari Bhajan Pavitra Na Hwaihai, Dhovau Aathau Yam.Kaaya Chhod Hans Udi Jaihai, Pado Rahai Dhan Dham. [2]Apno Sut Mukh Loo Dhar Dehai, Soch Lehu Parinam.‘Roopkunwari’ Sab Chhod Basahu Braj, Bhajiye Shyama Shyam. [3]- Sri Roop Kunwari JiWithout devotion to God, this body is useless — it is merely filled with filth like excrement and urine, and without bhajan (devotional worship), this fleshly form becomes completely fruitless. [1]Without Hari’s bhajan, no one can become truly pure, even if they cleanse themselves eight times a day.Ultimately, like a swan departing its lake, the soul will flee, leaving behind all wealth and kin. [2]One’s very own son will light the funeral pyre—ponder deeply over this truth. Sri Rupkunwari says: True fulfillment lies in abandoning everything, dwelling in Braj, and lovingly worshiping Shri Shyama-Shyam! [3]

title: Jo Man Arujhyo Roop Hain - Shri Nagridas Ji (Maharaj Savant Singh Ji) Ji Ki Vani, Manorath Manjari (30)
sanskrit_text: Jo Man Arujhyo Roop Hain, Kyon Hoo Kath Banain Na.Rasna Kain To Man Nahi, Man Kain Rasna Hain Na.- Shri Nagridas Ji, Shri Nagridas Ji Ki Vani, Manorath Manjari (30)The state of mind, entangled in the divine beauty (form) of Shyama Shyam, cannot be expressed in words, for the tongue has no mind, and the mind has no tongue to express itself.

title: Lage Jo Shree Ballabh Pad Rang - Goswami Shri Harirai Ji
sanskrit_text: (Raag Vihag)Lage Jo Shree Ballabh Pad Rang.Taakon Dushang Naik Nahi Vyapai, Aai Mile Satsang. [1]Shree Gobardhanadharan Dheer Ko, Dhyan Dharat Ang-Ang.‘Rasik’ Preetam Ki Baanik Upar, Baaron Koti Anang. [2]- Goswami Shri Harirai JiWhoever immerses themselves in the divine hue of Shri Vallabh’s (Lord Krishna or Shri Vallabhacharya) lotus feet remains untouched by bad association and naturally attains the company of saints. [1]He remains ever absorbed in meditating upon the beautiful limbs of Sri Giridhar Lal, the lifter of Govardhan. Goswami Shri Hariray Ji declares, “Even millions of Kamadevas pale before  the charm of Lord Krishna’s form.” [2]

title: Koau Kaami Krodhi Kaho Kou Lobhi Kaho Naun  - Shri Hita Damodar Das, Nem Battisi (9)
sanskrit_text: Koau Kaami Krodhi Kahau, Koau Lobhii Kaho Naaun.Shri Vrindavan Chhaandi Kai, Ant Na Kit Hun Jaaun.- Shri Hita Damodar Das, Nem Battisi (9)Some may call me lustful, others wrathful, and some may label me greedy—let them say what they wish. But I shall never leave Shri Vrindavan, no matter how much anyone may criticize me.

title: Jugulalaal Tori Paiyan Parata Haun - Shri Lalit Madhuri
sanskrit_text: (Raag Ghaton)Jugulalal Tori Paiyan Parata Haun Mo Tan Nek Niharau.Shreevanwas Daan Kin Deejai Chhinchhin Hot Khisaaro.Ausar Nahi Ausar Karanako Kalou Kaal Vistaaro.Lalitmadhuri Nitt Lahau Ras Charankamal Piy Pyaro.- Shri Lalit MadhuriO Divine Couple! I bow down at Your lotus feet—please cast just a little merciful glance upon me. Grant me the boon of residing in Shri Vrindavan Dham, for every moment wasted outside Vrindavan is a loss beyond measure. [1]There is no certainty of another opportunity as time is fleeting, and there is no reason to delay as the influence of Kali Yuga is growing stronger with each passing day.  Lalit Madhuri prays — “May I daily relish the divine nectar flowing from the lotus feet of my beloved Priya-Priyatam (divine couple).” [2]

title: Shri Swami Haridas Ko Dharm Sumer Saman - Shri Lalit Kishori Dev Ju Ki Vani, Siddhant Ki Saakhi (317)
sanskrit_text: Shri Swami Haridas Ko, Dharma Sumer Samaan.Aur Dharma Sab Doongri, Yahi Baat Parmaan.- Shri Lalit Kishori Dev, Shri Lalit Kishori Dev Ju Ki Vani, Siddhant Ki Saakhi (317)The supreme love-dharma of Swami Sri Haridas ji, the continuous and exclusive devotion to the eternal love-plays (nitya-vihara-rasa) of the Divine Couple (Sri Radha Krishn), stands like a Mount Sumeru. In comparison to this, all other various practices appear as insignificant as small hills.

title: Banai Bane Tumhari Baat - Shri Saras Madhuri Ji
sanskrit_text: Banai Bane Tumhari Baat.Shri Vrishabhanu Ray Ki Beti Yah Yash Jag Vikhyat. [1]Bina Hukam Tumhare Bajrani Toote Na Taru Paat.Purusharth Jete Sab Jhoothe Karo Kou Dinraat. [2]Neek Nazar Karunakara Dekhat Dukhi Sukhi Hojat.Sarasamadhuri Seva Ko Sukh Vilse Bib Gun Gaat. [3]- Shri Saras MadhuriO Kishori Radhe! Only through Your grace can the misfortune of a soul be rectified. O daughter of Shri Vrishabhanu, this glory of Yours is renowned throughout the world. [1]O Queen of Vraja! Without your command, not even a single leaf from a tree can fall. No matter how much a person strives day and night, without your grace, all efforts remain fruitless. [2]With just one merciful glance from You, even the most fallen attain supreme bliss. Sarasa Madhuri sings Your divine glories and prays to relish the bliss of serving You. [3]

title: Mulaprakrritirupam Tvam Bhajamah - Devi Bhagwat (9.50.50)

title: Shri Vipin Raj Maharaj Pranat Palan - Shri Ali Madhuri Ji, Shri Nikunj Keli Madhuri,  Shri Vrindavan Ju Ki Vinay Patrika (25)
sanskrit_text: Shri Vipin Raj Maharaj Pranat Palan Yah Naam Tiharau Hai.Jaan Ajaan Sharan Ko Jaise Balak Maatu Dulaarau Hai.Manvaan Chhit Phaladeya Sabhan Ko Kotik Surataru Waraau Hai.Prem Pravah Rasikjan Pyaare, Tinkau Praan Pyaarau Hai.Aleemadhuri Ke Jeevandhan Aadi Ant Rakhwaarau Hai.- Shri Ali Madhuri Ji, Shri Nikunj Keli Madhuri, Shri Vrindavan Ju Ki Vinay Patrika (25)O King of Forests, O supremely divine Shri Vrindavan Dham! You are known as “Pranatapal”—the Protector of the Surrendered. [1]Just like a mother embraces her child with unconditional love, whether the child understands it or not, You too shower grace upon all, whether they know you deeply or not. [2]You fulfill every desire of everyone and are more precious than millions of wish-fulfilling trees (Kalpatarus). [3]You are the source of life for the loving rasik devotees who are immersed in the stream of divine love (prema pravāha) because of you. [4]Shri Ali Madhuri Ji says: O sweet Vrindavan Dham! You are my entire life-wealth, and the only eternal protector, from beginning to end. [5]

title: Kain Tuv Kaan Pare Nahin Deenbandhu Mam Ter - Braj Ke Dohe
sanskrit_text: Kain Tuv Kaan Paree Nahin, Deenbandhu Mam Ter.Chaar Jugan Suni Chaar Bhuj, Lagi Na Etee Der.- Braj Ke DoheO friend of the destitute, O Shri Krishna! It seems my call has not reached Your ears—for in the four ages, you have never delayed in rescuing the fallen. Had you truly heard me, surely by now you would have delivered me, as always before. Perhaps the fault lies within me—I have not yet truly recognized myself as destitute, nor cried out to You from the depths of my heart.

title: Pran Diyai Yah Prem Na Paiyai - Shri Hita Dhruvdas, Bayalees Leela, Padyavali (98)
sanskrit_text: (Raag Kanharau)Pran Diyai Yah Prem Na Paiyai,Aisau Mahangau Ahi Sakhi Ree, Kahi Dhoon So Kaisai Kain Laiyai.Laal-Laadilee Kau Yah Sarvasu, Tihin Ras Kau Lalachaiyai.Adbhut Chhavi Vivi Ras Ki Dhara, ‘Dhruv’ Man Tahan Nhavaiyai.- Shri Hita Dhruvdas, Bayalees Leela, Padyavali (98)O dear friend! Even by offering one’s very life, this supreme love for Ladilī Lāl (Shri Radha-Krishna) is not attained. Such is the extraordinary and priceless nature of this divine love. So, O friend! You tell me—how can such love be obtained? [1]This selfless ‘Tatsukhmaya’ (giving happiness to the beloved) love is the highest treasure and the very source of life of Sri Radha Krishn themselves. In truth, there is no method or discipline by which it can be achieved—it is only through a deep longing (lolasā) for this divine rasa that one begins to qualify. Shri Dhruv Das ji says that a seeker, therefore, must develop detachment from all else and fully immerse the mind in the wondrous stream of rasa flowing from the divine form of the Divine Couple. [2]

title: Kadambarudham Ya Nijapatimajanam- Shri Vitthalnath Ji, Shri Swaminiyashtakam (7)
sanskrit_text: Kadambarudham Ya Nijapatimajanamtyahani Tat Tale Kurvamti Svapriyatamasakhibhih Saha Katham. Akasmadudvikshya Sphutataralaharorasamati Smitasmeravridananamuditadrrik Sa Mama Gatih.- Shri Vitthalnath Ji (Gusain Ji), Shri Swaminiyaashtakam (7)Unaware that Her Beloved had climbed the branches of the Kadamba tree, Sri Radha was immersed in a heartfelt conversation with Her sakhi about His glories when the pangs of separation overtook Her. As she looked around in longing, her gaze suddenly turned upward—and upon seeing Her Beloved, Her lotus-like face blushed with shyness and divine love-bliss. May such Shri Radha be my ultimate refuge.

title: Shri Kunjbihari Kau Jas Neeko - Shri Radha Prasad Dev Ju
sanskrit_text: Shri Kunjbihari Kau Jas Neeko,Jasu Naam Jag Bhakti Kalpataru, Sada Sukhad Sabhi Kau.Syama Syam Sneh Sachoti, Aur Jagat Sab Feeko.Shri Radha Prasad (Beg) Lejai Ab, Saran Ladili Ji Kau.- Shri Radha Prasad Dev JuThe glory of Shri Kunj Bihari is supremely enchanting. His name is like a wish-fulfilling tree of devotion in this world, always bestowing joy to all. [1]The divine love of Shyama-Shyam is the ultimate truth; everything else pales in comparison. Therefore, Shri Radha Prasad says, “Seek the shelter of Shri Radha’s lotus feet without delay.” [2]

title: Kavadhau Sevakunj Mein - Shri Lalit Kishori, Abhilash Madhuri, Vinay (56)
sanskrit_text: Kavadhau Sevakunj Mein, Hvaihon Shyamatamal.Latika Kargahi Viramihain, Lalit Ladaitilal.- Shri Lalit Kishori, Abhilash Madhuri, Vinay (56)When will I become a dark Tamal tree in the sacred Seva Kunj of Shri Vrindavan, so that the Divine Couple, Shri Shyama-Shyam, may rest while holding my tender vines during their love-filled leelas?

title: Mohan Tadag Bag Phool Phal Mohan Hain - Shri Hare Krishnanand Sarasvati, Vrindavan Shatak (14)
sanskrit_text: (Kavitt)Mohan Tadag Bag Phool Phal Mohan Hain,Mohan Gaay Giri Govardhan Lalam Hai. [1]Mohan Man Mohan Dhar Bahai Yamuna Ki,Mohan Madhupuri Mohan Nand Gram Hai. [2]Mohan Hain Gopijan Gwal Bal Mohan Hain,Mohan Shri Radha Aur Mohan Shri Shyam Hai. [3]Mohan Hain Lata Pata Kunj Sab Mohan Hain,Mohan Swaroop Yah Vrindavan Dham Hai. [4]- Dandi Swami Shri Hare Krishnanand Sarasvati ‘Hare Krishn’, Vrindavan Shatak (14)The enchanting lakes, blooming gardens, and their fruits and flowers — all captivate the heart; the gentle cows, the majestic Govardhan Hill — everything in this sacred land is enchanting. [1]The flowing waters of Yamunā hold an irresistible charm. Mathurā and Nandgaon all radiate divine enchantment. [2]The Gopīs and the young cowherd boys embody divine enchantment. Śrī Rādhā and Śrī Śyām Themselves are the very essence of this divine charm. [3]Vines, leaves, and every kuñj are enchanting, for the entire land of Vṛndāvan is an embodiment of divine enchantment, a manifestation of Śrī Kṛṣṇa Himself. [4]

title: Gaurangi Gunanidhi Priya Sakal Kala Ki Khaan - Shri Kishori Ali, Radha Namavali (10)
sanskrit_text: Gaurangi Gunanidhi Priya, Sakal Kala Ki Khaan.Garbeeli Gaj Gamini, Vidyagaan Nidan.- Shri Kishori Ali, Radha Namavali (10)Fair-complexioned Shri Radha is the treasure of all divine virtues and the source of all arts. title: Pyaro Pyari Jhoole Kadam Ki Dariyan - Sri Purushottam Ji
sanskrit_text: Pyaro Pyari Jhoole Kadam Ki Dariyan.Ghanaj Garaje Damini Damke, Chahoon Dish Gop Kumariyan. [1]Gaur Shyam Mukhchand Paraspaar, Rahat Nihar Nihariyan.‘Purushottam’ Prabhuki Chhabi Nirakhat, Chhabi Par Balhaariyan. [2]- Sri Purushottam JiBoth beloveds, Sri Radha Krishna, swing together on the branches of the Kadamba trees. Thunder roars, lightning flashes in the sky, and all around, the young gopis gather in joy. [1]The fair and dark faces of the divine couple gaze at each other lovingly. The gopis, enchanted by their supreme beauty, offer themselves again and again upon that divine vision. [2]

title: Dukh Taji Sukh Ki Chah Nahin - Shri Dayabai (a disciple of Shri Charan Das Ji of the Shuk sect.)
sanskrit_text: Dukh Taji Sukh Ki Chah Nahin, Nahin Vaikunth Vevan.Charan Kamal Chit Chahat Haun, Mohi Tumhari Aan.- Shri Dayabai (a disciple of Shri Charan Das Ji of the Shuk sect.)Dayabai says, “O Lord, I swear by You—let me be immersed in sorrow forever, I do not long for happiness, nor do I desire even Vaikuntha. I only wish that my mind may remain constantly and solely fixed on Your lotus feet.”

title: Kshan Bhangur Jeevan Ki Kalika - Braj Ke Sawaiya
sanskrit_text: Kshan Bhangur Jeevan Ki Kalika, Kal Prat Ko Jaane Khili Na Khili.Malayachal Ki Sheetal Aru Mand, Sugandh Sameer Chali Na Chali. [1]Kali Kaal Kuthaar Liye Phirta, Tan Namr Hai Chot Jhili Na Jhili. Le Le Harinaam Meri Rasana, Phir Ant Samay Ye Hili Na Hili. [2]- Braj Ke SawaiyaThe blossom of this fleeting life may or may not bloom tomorrow morning. The cool, fragrant breeze from the Himālaya may or may not be felt. [1]Kaliyug keeps its axe sharpened to strike down the human body. So let my tongue constantly chant the holy name of Hari, for this opportunity may not return. [2]

title: Yamuna Pulin Subhag Vrindavan - Shri Nanddas, Nanddas Granthwali
sanskrit_text: (Raag Sarang)Yamuna Pulin Subhag Vrindavan,Naval Lal Shrigovardhan Dhari. [1]Naval Kunj Naval Van Kusumit,Naval Naval Vrishbhanu Dulari. [2]Naval Haas Naval Chhabi Kridat,Naval Hulaas Karat Sukhkari. [3]Naval Shri Viththalnath Kripabal,Nandadas Nirakhat Balihari. [4]- Shri Nanddas, Nanddas GranthwaliThe ever-fresh Yamuna bank of the beautiful Shri Vrindavan Dham is extremely enchanting, where the newly adorned Shyamasundar, the lifter of Govardhan, resides. [1]The groves too are ever-new, covered with forest blossoms, where the ever-youthful daughter of Vrishabhanu, Shri Radha, is gracefully seated. [2]The ever-fresh sights of their sweet laughter, loving teasing, and playful pastimes captivate the mind. The Divine Couple is immersed in nectar-filled love-plays, showering bliss in all directions. [3]Ever-fresh too is Shri Vitthalnath Ji seated there; and by his grace, Shri Nanddas Ji beholds the Divine Couple and, relishing this wondrous rasa, offers himself again and again in surrender. [4]

title: Chal Man Vrindavan Chal Rahiye - Shri Shyamdas
sanskrit_text: Chal Man Vrindavan Chal Rahiye.Param Puneet So Braj Ki Dharani, Raj Dhari Sheesh Janam-Phal Lahiye. [1]Manjul Saghan Pulin Yamunatat, Sundar Parn-Kuti Chali Chhaiye.Sant Took Lahi Paay Yamuna Jal, Mili Rasikan Radhagun Gaiye. [2] Viharat Aavahin Yugalalal Jab, Man Ki Vyatha Katha Sab Kahiye. 'Shyam' Kripa Aisi Kab Kariho, Chali Vrindavan Laut Na Aiye. [3]- Shri ShyamdasO mind, reside eternally in Vrindavan, where the  land is supremely sanctified by the lotus feet of Sri Shyama Shyam. Adorn your forehead with this dust to attain the fruits of countless lifetimes. [1]In that forest adorned with dense, beautiful trees on the banks of the Yamuna, build a charming leaf hut and dwell there. Sustaining ourselves with the remnants of saints and the water of the Yamuna, let us sing the glories of Shri Radha in the company of rasik devotees. [2]When the youthful couple, Sri Shyama Shyam, come wandering through the groves, pour out all your heart to them. O Sri Shyama Shyam, when will you grace me such that I may never have to return from Vrindavan? [3]

title: Pandit Ya Ras Tain Bache - Shri Biharin Dev Ji Ki Vani, Siddhant Ki Saakhi (322)
sanskrit_text: Pandit Ya Ras Tain Bache, Jyon Bijhukai Mrig Rojh.Navai Na Achavan Paavahi, Ved Ladai Sir Bojh.- Shri Biharin Dev Ji, Shri Biharin Dev Ji Ki Vani, Siddhant Ki Saakhi (322)Pandits (Scholars) flee from the path of pure, love-filled rasa-bhakti like deer run away from a scarecrow in a lush field. Burdened by scriptural rules and intellectual pride, they lack the humility needed to enter the realm of divine love—without which, true prem-bhakti can never awaken.

title: Nirakhi Nirakhi Ali Roop Lubhaani - Shri Albeli Ali, Samay Prabandh (59)

title: Astih Mathura Naam Trishu Lokeshu Vishruta - Saur Puran
sanskrit_text: Astih Mathura Naam Trishu Lokeshu Vishruta.Krishn Paadrajomishr Vaaluka Poot Veethika.Sparshena Raajasastasy Muchyate Janmabandhanaat.- Saur PuranThere is a place named Mathura, renowned across all three worlds, where the pathways are sanctified by the dust of Shri Krishna’s lotus feet. By merely touching that divine dust, one becomes freed from the bondage of birth and death.

By merely touching that divine dust, one becomes frid from the bondage of birth and death.

title: Jog Jagy Jap Tap Teerath Gavan Vrat - Shri Lal Balbir Ji, Braj Binod, Shri Radha Shatak (105)
sanskrit_text: (Kavitt)Jog Jagy Jap Tap Teerath Gavan Vrat,Kabahun Na Haridas Shravan Katha Kari. [1]Bhramana Bhramayau Maya Moh Mad Liptaayau,Vrithan Jag Baadan Mein Umar Bita Kari. [2]Lal Balbir Mati Heen Main Malin Peen,Sewa Rasikan Tanhoon Ki Nahin Ja Kari. [3]Krishn Ali Ju Ki Kripa Drishti Bar Paay Paay,Radha Thakurayan Ke Paayan Ki Chaakari. [4] - Shri Lal Balbir Ji, Braj Binod, Shri Radha Shatak (105)Neither did I perform yogic practices, sacrifices, chanting, austerities, or pilgrimages, nor did I ever listen to the sacred stories of Lord Hari. [1]Wandering aimlessly, entangled in illusion, bound by attachment and ego, I wasted my whole life in useless worldly debates. [2]Foolish, impure, and steeped in sorrow, not even once did I serve the true rasika devotees. [3]Yet by the mere glimpse of grace from Kṛṣṇa Ali Jū, my beloved Gurudev, I have been blessed to become a humble maidservant at the lotus feet of Śrī Rādhā Thākuraṇī. [4]

title: Phiri-Phiri Radha-Krishn Kahi - Braj Ke Dohe
sanskrit_text: Phiri-Phiri Radha-Krishn Kahi, Phiri-Phiri Dhyan Lagayi.Phirihaun Kunjan Be-Phikar, Kab Brindavan Jayi.- Braj Ke DoheRepeating again and again—“Shri Radha-Krishna, Shri Radha-Krishna”—with my heart absorbed solely in their remembrance, when will I roam carefree through the groves of Shri Dham Vrindavan, fully immersed in their divine love?

title: Priya Tere Charan Kamal Ki Cheri - Shri Hita Gopal Das [Of Sewa Kunj], Nikunj Ras Vallari
sanskrit_text: Priya Tere Charan Kamal Ki Cheri.Kunj Dwaar Pai Thaadi Kab Son, Karo Nahin Ab Deri. [1]Kripa Karo Ab Jhalak Dikhaavo, Ye Abhilaasha Meri.Seva Kunj Nikunj Bhavan Mein, Nit Hi Karo Tum Pheri. [2]Daya Karo Ab Bhool Na Jaiyo, Rakhiyo Apni Cheri.Hit Gopal Ki Bhori Swaamini, Sun Lo Vinati Meri. [3]- Shri Hita Gopal Das [Of Sewa Kunj], Nikunj Ras VallariO Priya Ju (Shri Radha)! I am your humble maidservant. I have been standing at the entrance of the Kunj (the sacred grove), waiting for you—please, do not delay your mercy. [1]Please grant me just one glimpse of your divine form—this is my only desire. You eternally reside in Seva Kunj, that sacred forest of playful pastimes; kindly bless me with the opportunity to serve you there. [2]Now, please have compassion— do not forget me. Keep me forever as your devoted maidservant. O innocent and gracious Swamini of Shri Hit Gopal Das Ji, kindly hear this humble prayer of mine. [3]

title: Net Net Kahi Nigam Puni Jaahi Sakai Nahin Jaan - Shri Rasnidhi
sanskrit_text: Net Net Kahi Nigam Puni, Jaahi Sakai Nahin Jaan.Bhayo Manohar Aai Braj, Vahi So Hari Har Aan.- Shri RasnidhiThe Supreme Brahman, whom the Vedas describe with the words “neti neti,” beyond the reach, appeared in Braj as the all-attractive Lord Shri Krishna.

title: Shri Radhavallabh Ki Nav-Keerati - Shri Hariram Vyas, Vyas Vani, Purvardh (59)
sanskrit_text: (Raag Sarang)Shri Radhavallabh Ki Nav-Keerati Varnat Hu Na Nighaat.Bharatkhand Ki Su Kavimandali Varnat Hu Na Aghaat. [1]Bade Rasik Jaydev Vakhani Leela Amrit Chuchaat.(Shri) Vrindavan Harivansh Prasansit, Suni Gori Muskaat. [2]Raag Sahit Haridas Kahi Ras Nadi Bahi Na Thahaat.Rasik Ananyani Ki Joonthani ‘Vyas’ Sakhi, Ruchi Suchi Kai Khaat. [3]- Shri Hariram Vyas, Vyas Vani, Purvardh (59)The ever-new glories of the divine couple, Shri Radhavallabh, are beyond all description.Even the greatest poets of Bharat do not tire of describing the nectar of their divine love. [1]When the great rasik poet Jayadeva described these pastimes, it was as though a shower of nectar rained down.When Shri Harivansh praised Vrindavan, fair Sri Radha smiled with joy upon hearing it. [2]When Swami Shri Haridas sang this rasa with full raga and deep devotion, a river of divine nectar began to flow—vast and unfathomable.Sakhi Vyas (Hariram) lovingly partakes of the remnants (jūṭhan) left behind by such ‘Ananya’ (exclusive) Rasikas. [3]

title: Dekhi Deh Surang Yah Mati Bhule Man Mahi - Goswami Shri Harirai Ji, Vallabh Saakhi (38)
sanskrit_text: Dekhi Deh Surang Yah, Mati Bhule Man Mahi.Shri Vallabh Bin Aur Koou, Tero Sangi Nahi.- Goswami Shri Hariray Ji, Vallabh Saakhi (38)O mind! title: Vanraj Hamaare Pyare Hain - Shri Lalit Kishori Dev Ju Ki Vani, Siddhant Ke Pad (91)
sanskrit_text: Vanraj Hamaare Pyare Hain.Nity Sada Bhoo-Tal Par Raajat, Maha Prem Ras Bhaare Hain. [1]Jo Kachhu Ruchai Karain Ye Soi, Tan Man Ati Hitakaare Hain.Shri Kunjvihari Kau Niju Jeevan, Chhin Hoon Hot Na Nyare Hain. [2]- Shri Lalit Kishori Dev, Shri Lalit Kishori Dev Ju Ki Vani, Siddhant Ke Pad (91)Shri Dham Vrindavan, the King of Forests, is supremely dear to us (Rasikas). It eternally resides upon this earth and is the very source of divine love-bliss.  [1]Whatever is dear to the Divine Couple and Their devotees, Vrindavan nurtures and fulfils that very bhāva (divine sentiment). It is supremely auspicious for both body and mind. Shri Lalit Kishori Dev says: For Shri Kunj Bihari, Vrindavan is His very life and soul—He cannot bear to be separated from it even for a moment. [2]

title: Kaha Karu Kaason Kahun Ko Bujhe Kit Jaaun - Shri Madhuri Das, Utkantha Madhuri (29)
sanskrit_text: Kaha Karu Kaason Kahun, Ko Bujhe Kit Jaaun.Ban Ban Hi Dolat Phiron, Bolat Lele Naaun.- Shri Madhuri Das, Utkantha Madhuri (29)What should I do, whom should I tell, who will understand, where shall I go? With my heart burning in longing for a glimpse of the divine couple, Shri Radha Krishna, I roam the sacred groves of Vrindavan, crying out their names in desperation.

title: Poonam Ki Rajni Sajni Yah - Braj Ke Sawaiya
sanskrit_text: Poonam Ki Rajni Sajni Yah, Chandni Phail Rahi Sukhdani. [1]Yamuna Tat Pai Murli Suniken, Vrishbhanulali Ati Hi Sakuchani. [2]Raas Kiyau Hari Ke Sang Mein, Ati Chav Bhari Nahin Jaat Bakhani. [3]Auran Ki Parvah Nahin, Apani Thakurain Radhikarani. [4]- Braj Ke SawaiyaO sakhī (friend), it is the night of the full moon, and soothing moonlight spreads all around, bestowing great bliss. [1]Hearing the sweet melody of Śrī Kṛṣṇa's flute on the banks of Yamunā, Vṛṣabhanu Nandini Śrī Rādhā became extremely restless. [2]Immersed deeply in love, Śrī Rādhā performed the great Mahārāsa pastimes with Śrī Kṛṣṇa, whose beauty and sweetness I find impossible to describe. [3]I do not care for anyone else, as my sole protectress, my Ṭhākurāṇī, is Śrī Rādhārāṇī alone. [4]

title: Munchantyashruni Sarvyastu - Shri Vanshi Ali, Sri Radha Siddhant (26)
sanskrit_text: Munchantyashruni Sarvyastu Krishnopyashruni Munchati.Premnanddhastathapishta Rupmatt Gajenahi.- Shri Vanshi Ali, Sri Radha Siddhant (26)Shri Radha’s transcendental beauty, like a wild and majestic elephant, has trampled all—binding Her intimate sakhis and Shri Krishna Himself in the ropes of Her love, leaving them with no choice but to shed tears of love, endlessly, in divine ecstasy.

title: Nav Kishori Nav Kishor Bani Hai Vichitra Jori - Shri Chaturbhuj Das
sanskrit_text: (Raag Malhar)Nav Kishori Nav Kishor Bani Hai Vichitra Jori.Sobha Sindhu Madan Mohan Roop Rasi Kamini. [1]Rajat Tan Gaur Shyam Pyari Piy Bhaag Baam.Nav Ghan Giridharn Ang Sang Manu Damini. [2]Pahire Pat Peet Raate Bhushan Bhushit Manohar.Gaj Bar Gopal Nagar Nagari Gaj Gamini. [3]‘Daas Chaturbhuj’ Dampati Upma Kahan Nahin Auru.Kaam Murati Kamal Lochan Mrignayani Kamini. [4]- Shri Chaturbhuj DasThe ever-youthful Kishori (Radha) and ever-youthful Kishor (Krishna) is a wondrously beautiful divine couple. Shri Krishna, the enchanter of Cupid, is an ocean of elegance, and Shri Radha is the very embodiment of beauty. [1]With a radiant golden form (Radha) and a dark, cloud-like complexion (Krishna), they appear like lightning embraced by a monsoon cloud. [2]Draped in yellow garments and adorned with charming ornaments, the divine pair shines resplendently. Krishna, the master of all, walks beside Radha, whose gait is as graceful as that of a royal elephant (gaj-gāminī). [3]Sri Chaturbhujdas says: There is no comparison to this divine couple. They are the very embodiment of love, with lotus eyes and the enchanting, doe-like glances of Kamini Radha. [4]

title: Raksha Kari Na Jeev Ki Diyo Na Aadar Daan - Shri Narayan Swami, Anurag Ras (78)
sanskrit_text: Raksha Kari Na Jeev Ki, Diyo Na Aadar Daan. Narayan Ta Purush Son, Rookh Bhalo Phalvaan.- Shri Narayan Swami, Anurag Ras (78)One who neither respects nor shelters another living being is worse than a tree—for even a tree selflessly gives shade and bears fruit for others.

title: Shri Radharani Shrivan Drig Darsavo- Shri Lalit Kishori, Abhilash Madhuri, Vinay (15)
sanskrit_text: (Raga Jhanjhotī)Shri Radha Rani Shrivan Drig Darasavau.Ankit Pag Mag Dhoori Vepiki, Mam Angan Parasavau. [1]Lalit Kishori Rasik Lala Sang, Surati Rang Barsavau.Umahin Ghat Vijuriya Launkat, Jira Jini Tarasavau. [2]- Shri Lalit Kishori, Abhilash Madhuri, Vinay (15)O Shri Radharani, please grant me the divine vision of the sacred groves of Shri Vrindavan Dham. Let the dust of your lotus-marked feet, which has graced the forest pathways, touch and sanctify my entire being. [1]May you shower waves of divine love-sport along with your beloved Rasika Shyamasundara.  Do not leave this longing soul thirsting—reveal that very lightning-laced dark cloud of Your playful union. [2]

title: Vaikunthadi Padam Kamyamapi  - Shri Hita Krishn Chandra, Shri Radha Upsudha Nidhi (44)
sanskrit_text: Vaikunthadi Padam Kaamyamapi Tuchchham Matam Mama.Na Yatra Tvaamaham Vikshe Vrindaranya-Vilasini.- Shri Hita Krishn Chandra, Shri Radha Upsudha Nidhi (44)O Sri Radhe, who sports in the divine groves of Vrindavan! Wherever I do not behold Your darshan—even the highest abodes like Vaikunṭha are utterly insignificant and undesirable to me.

title: Shri Vrishabhan Kunavari Kripa Kari - Shri Kishori Ali
sanskrit_text: Shri Vrishabhan Kunavari Kripa Kari,Meri Or Nihaaro Ju. [1]Mose Heen Deen Kon Kar Gahi,Apanon Kari Prati Paaro Ju. [2]Gaavat Harivansii Haridasi,Virad Prasidh Tiharo Ju. [3]Vanshi Ki Pahachani ‘Kishori’,Ab Jini Mohi Visaro Ju. [4]- Shri Kishori AliO beloved daughter of Vrishbhanu, Sri Radha! Please cast your merciful, compassionate glance upon me. [1]O protector of the helpless! Take hold of this lowly soul’s hand and, by any means, make me yours forever. [2]Sri Harivanshi (Sri Hita Harivansh) and Sri Haridasi (Swami Haridas) constantly sing of your glories — your fame resounds through all three worlds. [3]Sri Kishori Ali says, “Through the relation of Vanshi Ali, please be merciful and make me yours forever. And I pray — may you never abandon me, not even for a moment.” [4]

title: Paayan Pari Binati Kara - Shri Bhagwat Rasik Ki Vani, Ananyarasikabharan Granth (1.8)
sanskrit_text: Paayan Pari Binati Karai, Se Ras Mukhya Singaar,Maan Chhodi Mridu Bachan Kahi, Karuna Ras Niradhaar.- Shri Bhagwat Rasik, Shri Bhagwat Rasik Ki Bani, AnanyaRasikabharan Granth (1.8)When Shri Krishn humbly falls at Shri Radha’s feet and pleads with utmost tenderness, that very act becomes the essence of Śṛṅgāra Rasa (the divine sentiment of love). And when Shri Kishoriji, moved by His soft-hearted words, melts in compassion and abandons her loving anger (māna), speaking gentle, affectionate words in return—that defines Karuṇa Rasa (the mood of divine compassion).

title: Dhan Dhan Vrindavan Ki Maalin Pyari - Shri Abhay Ram, Vrindavan Rahasya Vinod (114)
sanskrit_text: Dhan Dhan Vrindavan Ki Maalin Pyari.Thakur Ke Darbaaje Baithi, Goonthay Maala Nyari. [1]Goonthay Haar Banaawai Turra, Karai Jeevka Bhaari.Abhayaram Ye Hu Badbhaagin, Syama Syam Ki Pyari. [2]- Shri Abhay Ram, Vrindavan Rahasya Vinod (114)Blessed, truly blessed is the gardener of Shri Vrindavan Dham!She sits at the Lord’s doorway, stringing beautiful flower garlands with loving devotion. [1]She weaves garlands, turbans, and tassels of the Lord, earning a simple livelihood. Sri Abhayram says, she is truly fortunate, for she is very dear to the divine couple, Shri Shyama Shyam. [2]

[2]- Shri Abhay Ram, Vrindavan Rahasya Vinod (114)Blessed, truly blessed is the gardener of Shri Vrindavan Dham!She sits at the Lord’s durway, stringing beautiful flower garlands with loving devotion. [1]She weaves garlands, turbans, and tassels of the Lord, earning a simple livelihud. Sri Abhayram says, she is truly fortunate, for she is very dear to the divine couple, Shri Shyama Shyam. [2]

title: Niranjanam Nirgunamadvitiyam  - Shri Vagish Shastri Ji, Shri Radha Saptashati (5.63)
sanskrit_text: Niranjanam Nirgunamadvitiyam Vadanti Tattvam Vibudhastathastu.Maya Tu Vrrindavanameva Tattvam Sunishchitam Shripadabhushitangam.- Shri Vagish Shastri Ji, Shri Radha Saptashati (5.63)The learned scholars declare the ultimate truth to be pure, attributeless, and non-dual—so be it. But as for me, I have accepted Shri Vrindavan alone as the Supreme Truth, for its soil is adorned with the sacred footprints of Sri Radha Maharani.

title: Preeti Ki Baaji Kheliye Pyari - Shri Bhori Sakhi, Prem Ki Peer (104)
sanskrit_text: Preeti Ki Baaji Kheliye Pyaari.Haun Tau Kaachi Preeti Lai Aayi, Saanchi Preeti Laau Sukunwaari.Haun Tau Baaji Avas Hi Haarihaun, Jeeti Karau Nij Aagyaakaari. [1]Aisi Cheri Karau Aapni, Chhin Na Haunu Charanan Tain Nyaari,Teri Sahaj Daan Par ‘Bhauri’, Baar-Baar Jaaun Balihaari. [2]- Shri Bhori Sakhi, Prem Ki Peer (104)O Beloved Priyaji! Please play this game of love with me. I fully know that my love is immature and Your love is pure and true; thus, it is certain that I shall lose and You shall win. But I humbly beg You—upon winning, kindly make me Your obedient maidservant. [1]Make me such a devoted and exclusive maidservant that I may never be separated from You, not even for a single moment. Shri Hit Bhori Sakhi says: “Upon receiving such a gracious gift of Your mercy, I offer myself to You, again and again, completely surrendered.” [2]

title: Ajgar Karai Na Chakri Panchhi Kare Na Kaam - Shri Malook Das
sanskrit_text: Ajgar Karai Na Chakri, Panchhi Kare Na Kaam.Daas Malooka Kah Gaye, Sab Ke Data Ram.- Shri Malook DasThe python doesn’t serve anyone, and birds do no labor. Saint Malukadas says, “The Lord provides for all.”

title: Syam Sab Hi Ke Jiy Ki Jaanat Hain - Shri Biharin Dev Ju Ki Vani, Siddhant Ke Pad (107)
sanskrit_text: Syam Sab Hi Ke Jiy Ki Jaanat Hain,Karat Bhakti Vyopaar Lobh Lagi, Taahi Kaha Kachu Maanat Hain. Antarjaami Sabke Swaami, Sahaj Preeti Pahichanat Hain,Shri Bihariji Daas Nihkaam Man Ki Rati, Shreemukh Barin Bakhaanat Hain. - Shri Biharin Dev, Shri Biharin Dev Ju Ki Vani, Siddhant Ke Pad (107)Shri Banke Bihari Ji, the Lord of all and the one who resides within every being, knows the innermost thoughts of every heart. He is fully aware of even the subtlest emotions and intentions that arise in the mind. Those who engage in devotion driven by attachment or greed, treating devotion as a business, hold no value in His eyes. But He lovingly sings glories of those who love Him selflessly, without any desire for personal gain.

title: Lat Chhuti Triy Sheesh Te Rahi Kapolan Chhaay - Braj Ke Dohe
sanskrit_text: Lata Chhooti Triy Sheesh Te, Rahi Kapolan Chhaay.Maanau Chhauna Naag Kau, Pee Pee Ami Aghaay.- Braj Ke DoheLord Krishna says—Shri Radha’s curly locks cling to her lotus-like face as if many baby serpents, having drunk their fill of divine nectar, now lie in divine ecstasy.

title: Yugal Naam Saun Nem, Japat Nit Kunjbihari - Shri Nabhadas, Bhaktamala (91)
sanskrit_text: (Chhapay)Jugal Naam Saun Nem, Japat Nit Kunjbihari.Avalokat Rahain Keli, Sakhi Sukh Ke Adhikari. [1]Gaan Kala Gandharv, Shyam Shyama Kaun Toshain.Uttam Bhog Lagaay, Mor Marakat Timi Poshain. [2]Nripati Dvar Thaade Rahain, Darasan Aasa Jaas Ki.(Shri) Asudheer Udyotakar, Rasik Chhap Haridas Ki. [3]- Shri Nabhadas, Bhaktmaal (91)Describing the glory of Swami Srhi Haridas Ji, Nabhaji says -Swamiji’s unwavering principle was to constantly chant the names of the Yugal (Divine Couple) and remain immersed in the service of Shri Shyama Kunj Bihari.He perpetually beheld their intimate transcendental Keli plays and relished the inner rasa of being a confidential sakhi of Shri Radha. [1]Through his unparalleled mastery of music, he pleased the Divine Couple in such a way that even the most skilled Gandharvas seemed ordinary before him.Each day, he offered an array of bhoga (food offerings), and the remnants (prasāda) were lovingly given to nourish the peacocks, monkeys, and aquatic creatures of Vrindavan. [2]While residing in Nidhivan, even kings and dignitaries would wait patiently outside his kutira, longing for a mere glimpse of him. Glorifying the noble lineage of Shri Ashudhir Ji, Swami Haridas Ji shines as the crest jewel of all rasikas, the foremost among the lovers of divine rasa. [3]

title: Sut Tiy Grih Dhan Raajy Hu - Shri Bhartendu Harishchandra, Bhartendu Granthawali, Bhakta Sarvasva (7)
sanskrit_text: Sut Tiy Grih Dhan Raajy Hu, Ya Mein Sukh Kachhu Nahin.Parmanand Prakaas Ek, Krishna-Charan Ke Maahin.- Shri Bhartendu Harishchandra, Bhartendu Granthawali, Bhakta Sarvasva (7)Neither son nor wife, home nor wealth, not even a vast kingdom can offer true happiness. Supreme happiness is found only at the lotus feet of Shri Krishna.

Supreme happiness is found only at the lotus fit of Shri Krishna.

title: Jo Mann Naari Ki Or Nihaarat - Shri Sundar Ji
sanskrit_text: (Sawaiya)Jo Mann Naari Ki Or Nihaarat, Tau Man Hot Hai Taahi Ko Rupa. [1]Jo Man Kaahu So Krodh Karai Jab, Krodhmayi Ho Jaai Tadrupa. [2]Jo Man Maaya Hi Maaya Rate Nit, Tau Man Doobat Maaya Ke Kupa. [3]Sundar Jau Man Brahm Vichaarat, Tau Man Hot Hai Brahmswarupa. [4]- Shri Sundardas JiA mind that constantly gazes upon women with sensual intent becomes absorbed in that very form — it takes on the nature of sensuality itself. [1]A mind that gets angry takes the form of anger itself. [2]If the mind is always absorbed in material illusion (māyā), then it drowns in the deep well of illusion. [3]But if the mind contemplates the Supreme Brahman, then it transforms and becomes of the very nature of Brahman itself. [4]

title: Shri Vrindavan Ras Sudha - Shri Ramray, Geet Govind Braj Bhasha, Doha (81)
sanskrit_text: Shri Vrindavan Ras Sudha, Sindhu Nimajjat Joy.Tako Teeno Taap Ko, Kabahu Taap Nahin Hoy.- Shri Ramray, Geet Govind Braj Bhasha, Doha (81)One who immerses themselves in the nectarean ocean of Shri Vrindavan’s divine rasa never again experiences the threefold material miseries—daihika (intrinsic), daivika (superhuman), and bhautika (extrinsic).
english_text: Shri Vrindavan Ras Sudha, Sindhu Nimajjat Joy.Tako Tino Tap Ko, Kabahu Tap Nahin Hoy.- Shri Ramray, Git Govind Braj Bhasha, Doha (81)One who immerses themselves in the nectarean ocean of Shri Vrindavan’s divine rasa never again experiences the thrifold material miseries—daihika (intrinsic), daivika (superhuman), and bhautika (extrinsic).

title: Mo Sam Kaun Kutil Avichari - Shri Lalit Ladaiti, Shri Kishori Kripa Kataksha, Vinay (11)
sanskrit_text: (Raag Paraj Va Khmmach)Mo Sam Kaun Kutil Avichaari,Jihin Rasna Ras Naam Tyaag Ke, Nishidin Baatein Bakat Labaari. [1]Je Akhiyaan Taj Yugal Roop Ras, Chhaki Rahat Nit Neh Sut-Naari, Je Kar Dampati Charan Palotat, Lage Haran Pardhan Dukh Bhaari. [2]Nishidin Aas Vaas Vrindavan, Roop Sudhaaras Peevau Pyaari,Kripa Drishti Dukh Hero Mo Tan, Lalit Ladeti Sharan Tihari. [3]- Shri Lalit Ladaiti, Shri Kishori Kripa Kataksha, Vinay (11)Who could be more wicked and thoughtless than me, who abandoned the nectar-like name from the tongue and instead wastes day and night in meaningless chatter? [1]These eyes, meant for beholding the nectarine beauty of the Divine Couple, are instead intoxicated by worldly attachments of sons and wife. These hands, which were meant to serve the lotus feet of the couple lovingly, are instead used to grasp the wealth of others, becoming burdened with sin. [2]Now my only hope is to reside in Shri Vrindavan and drink the beauty of Pyariju (Sri Radha) with every breath. Shri Lalit Ladaiti cries, “O sweet Radha, I am surrendered unto You—please grace me with Your merciful glance and dispel all my sorrows.” [3]

title: Praan Jeevan Ke Neh Mein Tan Mann Se Rahe Chur - Shri Roop Madhuri Ji Ki Vani, Rasik Pacchisi (10)
sanskrit_text: Praan Jeevan Ke Neh Mein, Tan Man Se Rahe Choor,Ghar Men Kai Ban Men Rahen, Soi Rasikjan Soor.- Shri Roopmadhuri, Shri Roop Madhuri Ji Ki Vani, Rasik Pacchisi (10)One whose body and mind remain immersed in the love of his Beloved Lord is the true (courageous) rasika. Whether He stays in a household or the forest, his heart remains forever absorbed in that divine love.

title: रसना कटौ जो अन रटौ - श्री हित स्फुट वाणी (24)
sanskrit_text:
"रसना कटौ जो अन रटौ"
- श्री हित हरिवंश महाप्रभु

मेरी जिह्वा कट जाए यदि में श्री राधा नाम के अलावा कुछ और रटन करूँ।
english_text: "rasana katau jo an ratau" - shri hit harivnsh mahaprabhu meri jihva kat jae yadi men shri radha nam ke alava kuchh aur ratan karun.

title: Lochan Bhaye Syam Ke Chere - Shri Surdas, Sura Sagara
sanskrit_text: (Raag Ramkali)Lochan Bhaye Shyam Ke Chere,Aite Pai Sukh Paavat Kotik, Motan Pheri Na Here. [1]Haaha Karat Parat Hari Charanani, Aise Bas Bhaye Unhi,Unko Badan Vilokat Nisi-Din, Merau Kahyo Na Sunhi. [2]Lalit Tribhangi Chhavi Par Atke, Phatke Moson Tori,‘Sur’ Dasa Yah Meri Kinhī, Aapun Hari Saun Jori. [3]- Shri Surdas, Sura SagaraMy eyes have become servants of the enchanting form of Shyamasundar. In this sweet bondage, they find such joy that they no longer even glance back at me. [1]I begged them, prayed at the Lord’s lotus feet, but they remain forever lost in His darshan, deaf to my voice. [2]So enchanted are they by His elegant ‘tribhangi’  (threefold-curved) form that they’ve broken all ties with me. Shri Surdas says: These eyes, devoted only to Him, have left me utterly helpless. [3]

title: Gati Garaveeli Dekhi Ke Maanat Man Mein Laaj - Shri Sanket Ali, Sanket Lata (92)
sanskrit_text: Gati Garaveeli Dekhi Ke, Maanat Man Mein Laaj,Yaahi Te Lai Dhoori Nij, Shir Daarat Gajaraj.- Shri Sanket Ali, Sanket Lata (92)Upon seeing the graceful and majestic gait of Shri Radharani, even the mighty king of elephants feels ashamed within himself. So subdued is he that he humbly bows down, takes the dust of Her feet, and places it upon his head—honoring the Queen of Vrindavan with all his pride cast aside.

title: Shri Bishok Nandini Binu Kau Hai - Shri Vanshi Ali, Siddhant Ke Pad (37)
sanskrit_text: Shri Bishok Nandini Binu Kau Hai,Ham Se Adham Aur Nirbahak, Yah Jas Aur Ko Sohai. [1]Jaako Man In Pad Ras Lagyau, So Kyon Sakai Ik Chhin Kavi Chhohai.Jai Shri Bansi Ali Shri Radha, Jeevan Dhan Jako Badan Kunwari Nit Jauhai. [2]- Shri Vanshi Ali, Siddhant Ke Pad (37)Who, other than Shri Bishok Nandini (Shri Lalita Sakhi), could uplift and sustain a fallen soul like me? Such unparalleled mercy and divine glory befit only her, for no one else could carry such grace. [1]One whose heart is deeply immersed in the nectar of Shri Lalita Sakhi’s lotus feet can never be deprived of her grace, even for a moment—because she is the living embodiment of Radha-prem, the divine love for Shri Radharani. Shri Vamshi Ali Ji says—“All glories to Shri Lalita Sakhi, for whose soul, very breath, and all wealth of life, Shri Radharani alone is everything. It is her lotus face that ever-youthful Sri Radha constantly beholds with love.” [2]

Such unparalleled mercy and divine glory befit only her, for no one else could carry such grace. [1]One whose heart is diply immersed in the nectar of Shri Lalita Sakhi’s lotus fit can never be deprived of her grace, even for a moment—because she is the living embodiment of Radha-prem, the divine love for Shri Radharani. Shri Vamshi Ali Ji says—“All glories to Shri Lalita Sakhi, for whose soul, very breath, and all wealth of life, Shri Radharani alone is everything. It is her lotus face that ever-youthful Sri Radha constantly beholds with love.” [2]
author: Braj Rasik Heritage
