title: Radhe Dai Vrindavan-Vaas - Shri Anandghan Ji, Shri Ghanananda Granthavali, Padavali (372)
sanskrit_text: (Raag Sarang Chautala)Radhe Dai Vrindavan-Vaas,Tero Hvai Man Panihi Pari Rahai, Tanhun Taahi Paas. [1]Mahaa Madhur Ras Keli-Maadhuri, Phurai Hiyai Anayaas,Hari Khari Sukh Bhari Nikunjai, Nau Nau Rang-Vikaas. [2]Jamuna-Teer Lalit Bansi-Dhuni, Adbhut Ami-Nivaas,Kripa-Ramand Ghamandani Aanandghan, Begi Puriyai Aas. [3]- Shri Anandghan Ji, Shri Ghanananda Granthavali, Padavali (372)O Sri Radhe, please grant me residence in Vrindavan! Let my mind become yours and remain surrendered like a water-carrier’s pot balanced on the head; let even my body stay close in your service in Vrindavan. [1]In the heart, may the sweetness of the divine love-sports (ras-keli) of the Yugal (Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa) arise effortlessly. In the intimate groves (nikunja), each day brings forth newer and newer colorful expressions of bliss. [2]On the banks of Yamuna, with the enchanting melody of Kṛṣṇa’s flute, dwells an extraordinary nectar-filled abode. O Shri Radhe! Please shower your mercy swiftly and fulfill this deep yearning of mine by granting me residence in that eternal Vrindavan. [3]

title: Bhaktaanaananda Sandoha - Sanat Kumar Samhita, Sri Radha Strotam (3)

title: Besar Kaun Ki Ati Niki - Shri Hita Damodar Das
sanskrit_text: (Raag Adano and Dhanashree)Besar Kaun Ki Ati Niki.Hodpari Laalan Aru Lalna Chaump Badhi Ati Jee Ki. [1]Nyay Paryo Lalita Ke Aagein, Kaun Lalit Kaun Phiki.Jai Shridamodar hit Vilag Na Manon, Jhukan Jhuki Pyari Ju Ki. [2]- Shri Hita Damodar DasWhose nose-ring (beṣar) is more beautiful? This question sparked a playful rivalry between Sri Radha and Sri Krishna, intensifying the emotional excitement in their hearts. [1]Seeking a verdict, they turned to Shri Lalita Ji. Lalita Ji gently declares, “Please don’t mind, but Pyariju’s (Sri Radha’s) tilted beṣar holds a charm that cannot be surpassed.” [2]

title: Atki Naav Kuthaur Mein Padi Bhaunroo Bich Aay - Shri Ramswaroop Ji
sanskrit_text: Atki Naav Kuthaur Mein, Padi Bhaunroo Bich Aay.Aho Lali Vrishabhaan Ki, Tum Bin Kaun Sahaay.- Shri Ramswaroop Ji The boat of my life is trapped in the midst of a fierce whirlpool, on the verge of sinking. title: Yah Rasa Reeti Priya Priyatam Ki - Shri Bhagwat Rasik Ki Vani, Ananyarasikabharan Granth (12.7)
sanskrit_text: Yah Ras-Reeti Priya-Priyatam Ki, Dibya Swati-Jal Jaise.Bisayi, Gyani, Bhakt, Upasak, Prapat Sabko Kaise. [1]Kadali, Kamal, Papiha, Seepi, Paatra-Bhed Gun Taise.Bhagavat Beej Visamata Nahi, Bhoomi Bhaagya Phal Aise. [2]- Shri Bhagwat Rasik, Bhagwat Rasik Ki Vani, Ananyarasikabharan Granth (12.7)This divine ‘Rasa Reeti’ (mode of love) of the divine couple, Priya-Pritam—known as Nitya Vihar Rasa—is like raindrops from the dark Swati star. Just as that rain, when it reaches different receptacles, transforms accordingly— camphor in the banana tree, pollen in the lotus, life-force in the papihā bird, and a pearl in the oyster—so too does this pure rasa transform according to the heart (pātra) it touches.When this rasa is received, the worldly-minded (viṣayī) perceives it as sensuality, the spiritual intellectual (jñānī) sees it as knowledge, the devotee (bhakta) experiences devotion, and the rasika, the true connoisseur, drowns completely in divine love. Shri Bhagavatrāsika Ji explains that the seed of all bliss in the universe lies in the eternal play (nitya-vihār) of the divine couple, Shyama Kunja Bihari. The diversity of experiences arises not from the seed, but from the soil—that is, the preparedness and receptivity of each heart. Therefore, to truly partake in Nitya Vihar Rasa, one must become a rasika.

title: Tain Jo Ratan Paayo Bhalo Janyo Saadhi Na Saaj - Shri Surdas, Sura Sagara
sanskrit_text: Tain Jo Ratan Paayo Bhalo, Janyo Saadhi Na Saaj.Prem Katha Anudin Sunai, Tau Na Upjai Laaj.- Sri Surdas, Soor SagarYou’ve received the priceless, rare gift of human life, yet never learned its true worth. You hear tales of divine love each day, yet feel no shame for the emptiness of love within your heart.

sanskrit_text: (Kavitt)Roop Bhare Rang Bhare, Madhusmit Gandh Bhare,Bhare Makrand Mukhapankaj Mein Paag Rahe. [1]Mad Bhare Mod Bhare, Morpankh Sheesh Dhare,Kaare Ghunghraare Kach Kapolan Pai Laag Rahe. [2]Laad Bhare Lobh Bhare, Lochan Ve Loch Bhare,Karain Chugal Chhinih Shruti Mool Bhaag Rahe. [3]‘Prem’ Chit Bise Bhare, Jaay Ras Sabai Mare,Aiso Dhaam Shyaam Koou Mere Ur Jaag Rahe. [4]- Shri Prem JiFilled with divine beauty, colors of love, divine nectar, and fragrance, His lotus‑like face is soaked in the nectar of blissful expressions. [1]Filled with pride and divine intoxication, crowned in a peacock plume —His black curly hair gently sways upon His soft cheeks. [2]His eyes, full of affection and passion, speak without words —Their glance alone holds the Vedas’ deepest truths. [3]Prem Jī says: Such glimpses have taken root in my heart,A nectar that dissolves worldly pleasures, for Śyāmsundar, the abode of bliss, now dwells eternally in my heart. [4]

title: Vrindavan Sukh Ant Nahin Sthal Yugal Nivaas - Shri Lalit Ladaiti, Shri Kishori Kripa Kataksha, Madhurya Ras Dohavali (10)
sanskrit_text: Vrindavan Sukh Ant Nahin, Sthal Yugal Nivaas.Kamalapur Hooke Sadaa, Karat Aas Braj Vaas.- Shri Lalit Ladaiti, Shri Kishori Kripa Kataksha, Madhurya Ras Dohavali (10)There is no end to the bliss of Vrindavan, for it is the eternal abode of the ever-youthful divine couple, Shri Radha Krishna. Even Lord Hari, while residing in Kamalapur (the abode of Lakshmi, Vaikuntha), constantly longs to reside in the sacred land of Braj.

title: Muskyani Tihari Jo Maine Lakhi - Taj Begam
sanskrit_text: (Sawaiya)Muskyani Tihari Jo Maine Lakhi,Lakhi Ke Mann Mein Ati Neh Jutano. [1]Jo Tum Chahat Ek Bise,Hum Ek Ke Bees Bise Tehi Mano. [2]Raah Badi Hai Jo Prem Ke Panth Ki,Chatur Hoy Soi Chit Ano. [3]Jeevan Taj Kahe Jag Mein,Tuk Charahi Adi Ke Akshar Jano. [4]- Taj Begam (Taj Bibi)Tāj Bībī says—O Kṛṣṇa! Ever since I beheld Your sweet smile, my heart has been overflowing with love. [1]If You desire just one sentiment from me, know that I will cherish it as if it were twentyfold—I will value it immensely. [2]The path of divine love is not for the faint-hearted—it is deep, subtle, and often difficult. Only the wise, sincere, and truly loving-hearted can walk this path successfully. [3]The true essence of life lies in love itself. Whoever has understood love has understood the very meaning of existence. [4]

title: Abto Vasi Hriday Mo Mahin Vrajaraj Neh Lagaiye - Shri Lalit Madhuri
sanskrit_text: (Raag Ghaton)Abto Vasi Hriday Mo Maahin Vrajaraj Neh Lagaiye.Naate Neh Lok Ke Jete Te Manjh Dhaar Vahaiye.Aho Kishori Kahon Nihori Mohootan Chit Laiye.Lalitmadhuri Yehi Chahat Jugul Charan Darasaiye.- Shri Lalit MadhuriNow, the dust of Vraja (Vraj-raja) has made its eternal abode in my heart; my love is bound only to it. All worldly relationships and ties should now be cast away into the midstream. [1]O Kishoriji! I humbly beg for your merciful, sidelong glance. sanskrit_text: Jo Apne Augun Kahon, Paaoon Or Na Chhor,Antar Ki Janao Sabai, Syama Kaho Nihor.- Shri Ali Madhuri Ji, Shri Nikunj Keli Madhuri, Shri Radha Karunavali (8)If I begin to recount my faults, there would be no end to them. title: Lagi Meri Madan Mohan Se Yaari - Shri Roop Madhuri Ji Ki Vani, Padavali (136)
sanskrit_text: (Raag Shyamkalyan Va Bhairav)Lagi Meri Madan Mohan Se YaariMukut Latak Atki Ur Antar, Sabte Surta Taari [1]Basi Rahai Nit Nain Roop Chhavi, Pal Chhin Rahun MatwaariRoopmadhuri Guru Kripa Son, Jag Sukh Sakal Visaari [2]- Shri Roop Madhuri, Shri Roop Madhuri Ji Ki Vani, Padavali (136)My heart is now forever tied to my beloved Madan Mohan. The gentle swing of pearl strands from His slanted crown is etched so deeply within me, that it has erased all else. [1]His enchanting form now permanently dwells in my eyes, and I remain intoxicated in that vision. Shri Roop Madhuri says, “By my Guru’s mercy, I have cast aside all worldly attachments.” [2]

title: Pyari Nakh Chandan Kau Kijiye Chakor Man - Shri Premdas Ji Ki Vani (113)
sanskrit_text: (Kavitt)Pyari Nakh Chandan Kau Kijiye Chakor Mann,Radhe Gun Ganan Kau Pik Kar Dijiye [1]Phoole Pad Kanjan Kau Kariye Madhup Moi,Birad Bakhananbai Kau Koil Karijiye [2]Kijiye Maral Jo Pai Dijai Gati Aap Pyari,Kaiki Kar Kel Rel Shyam Ghan Bheejiye [3]Kijai Drum Beli Baag Shrivan Nikunjan Mein,Premsakhi Tu Hi Dhani Bhavai Taisi Kijiye [4]- Shri Premdas Ji [Brother of Shri Lal Balbir Ji], Shri Premdas Ji Ki Vani (93)Make my mind like a Chakora bird, ever thirsting for the moon‑like toenails of Priyājū (Śrī Rādhā), or transform me into a cuckoo, ever singing the sweet glories of Rādhe Jū. [1]Transform me into a bee, always hovering around the blossomed lotus feet of Śrī Rādhā, or make me a koel that constantly proclaims Her divine virtues aloud. [2]O Pyārījū, let me become a graceful swan who follows Your graceful gait, or a peacock who beholds Your love‑play with dark Śyāmsundar. [3]Turn me into the trees, creepers, and fragrant groves of Śrī Vṛndāvan’s Nikunj‑Van. Śrī Prem Sākhī prays — O Pyārījū, You alone are the true source of bliss, therefore, transform me into whatever pleases You. [4]

title: Shri Swami Haridas Ke Naval Nikunj Bihar - Shri Roop Sakhi, Siddhant Ke Doha (44)
sanskrit_text: Shri Swami Haridas Ke, Naval Nikunj Bihar.Chhavi Chheentein Chhahrat Hain, Tinke Dasa Avtar.- Shri Roop Sakhi, Siddhant Ke Doha (44)Shri Swami Haridasji’s beloved Banke Bihari, the one who performs Nitya Vihara in the Nikunjas is supreme among all. Only by receiving a mere sprinkle (reflection) of His divine beauty, even the ten incarnations (Dashavatar) find their radiance and manifestation.

title: Naval Kishori Gori Radha Gaiye - Shri Hita Parmanand Das
sanskrit_text: Naval Kishori Gori Radha Gaiye.Mohan Jeevan-Dhan Sakhiyan Pyari, Roop Drigan Darasaiye. [1]Apne Charan Kamal Ki Dasi, Yahai Aas Sarasaiye.‘Paramanand’ Hit Kripa Ravari, Hit Gulab Bali Paiye. [2]- Shri Hita Parmanand DasSing the divine glories of the fair-complexioned, ever-youthful Shri Radha! May I be blessed with her grace, so that the beloved of Shri Krishna, the one who steals the hearts of all the sakhis, reveals her divine form to me. [1]May it always remain my sole aspiration to attain eternal servitude at the lotus feet of Shri Radha and to be absorbed in her loving service. Shri Hit Parmanand Das Ji prays— “O Kishori Ji! Please bestow your mercy, and may I joyfully offer my very self like a blooming rose at your feet, forever surrendered.” [2]

title: Tasyobhayatati Ramya - Padma Purana, Section 5 [Patala Khand], Chapter 69, Verse 77, 78
sanskrit_text: Tasyobhayatati Ramya Shuddhakamchananirmita.Gamgakotiguna Prokta Yatra Sparshavaratakah.Karnikayam Kotiguno Yatra Kridarato Harih.Kalimdikarnika Krrishnamabhinnamekavigraham.- Padma Purana, Section 5 [Patala Khand], Chapter 69, Verse 77, 78Lord Shiva says to Goddess Parvati -Yamuna’s two banks located at Vrindavan are delightful, made of pure gold, and said to be millions of times more auspicious than the Ganges, where a mere touch grants supreme merit. In the pericarp, Hari (Krishna) engages in pastimes millions of times more delightful. The pericarp of the Yamuna and Krishna are non-different, embodying a single form.

title: Bani Dukool Baithe Parajank - Shri Rasik Dev Ji Ki Vani, Siddhant Ke Pad (17)
sanskrit_text: (Raag Vihagrau)Bani Dukool Baithe Parajank,Kamal Nain Ang Chhavi Nirkhat, Pyari Bhare Ju Ank. [1]Dhanya Dhanya Piy Maan Apanpau, Jyon Nidhi Paye Rank.Shri Rasik Bihari Yah Sukh Vilsat, Tahaan Nikat Nisank. [2]- Shri Rasik Dev Ji, Shri Rasik Dev Ji Ki Vani, Siddhant Ke Pad (17)Both beloveds, Shri Radha and Krishna, sit together adorned in fine silken garments. With lotus-like eyes, they gaze deeply into each other, and Pyariju (Sri Radha) embraces Him in the ecstasy of pure love-bliss. [1]The Beloved (Krishna) feels immensely blessed, like a pauper who has suddenly attained great treasure. In their private Nikunj palace, the divine couple, Bihari-Biharini delight in blissful plays of love, with no fear or hesitation in their nearness, says Sri Rasik Dev. [2]

title: Shyam Laal Baindi Bani Shobha Badi Apaar - Braj Ke Dohe
sanskrit_text: Shyam Laal Baindi Bani, Shobha Badi Apaar.Pragat Viraajat Sasin Par, Manu Anuraag Singaar.- Braj Ke DoheLord Krishna transforms himself into the red bindi (a decorative dot) on Sri Radha’s forehead, radiating limitless beauty. By becoming an ornament on her moonlike face, Shyamsundar expresses his deep love for Radha, making his presence a part of her adornment.

title: Shri Shyama Ju Ko Shyam Palotat Paam -  Shri Kripaluji, Prem Ras Madira, Shri Radha Madhuri (49)
sanskrit_text: Shri Shyama Ju Ko, Shyam Palotat Paam.Brahm Sachchidanand Nandasut, Jehi Kah Poorankam.Komal Kamal Lali Pag Laali, Lakhi Behaal Soi Shyam.Bali-Bali Jaat Lagaavat Nij Drig, Nij Kar Kamal Lalaam.Kabahun Hari Nij Ur Lapatavat, Charan Kamal Abhiram.Mridu Muskaay ‘Kripalu’ Vilokati, Latan Oat Brajabam.- Jagadguru Shri Kripalu Ji Maharaj, Prem Ras Madira, Shri Radha-Madhuri (49)Sri Shyamasundar gently presses the tender lotus feet of Shri Shyama Ju (Shri Radha). The very One whom the Vedas describe as eternally content and ‘Sachchidānanda’ has taken form as Nandanandan—the darling son of Nanda. [1]That same Nandanandan becomes completely overwhelmed upon seeing the redness of Kishoriji’s lotus feet. At times, He lovingly places Her feet upon His eyes, surrendering Himself completely. [2]At other times, Shyamasundar presses Her lotus feet to His heart with deep love and devotion. Shri Kripalu Ji says the maidens of Braj gaze upon this mesmerizing scene from behind the vines, smiling gently, captivated by its charm. [3]

title: Johan Nandakumar Kau Gai Nand Ke Geh - Shri Raskhan, Raskhan Ratnavali
sanskrit_text: Johan Nandakumar Kau, Gai Nand Ke Geh.Mohi Dekhi Muskai Ke, Barsyau Meh Saneh.- Shri Raskhan, Raskhan RatnavaliO Sakhi! I went to Nanda’s house to catch a glimpse of Shri Krishna. title: Shakti Nahi Dhruv Si Akhand Tap Kaise Karun - Shri Hare Krishnanand Sarasvati, Vrindavan Shatak (76)
sanskrit_text: (Kavitt)Shakti Nahi Dhruv Si Akhand Tap Kaise Karun,Bhakti Na Prahlad Si Ram Ram Kehne Ki. [1]Ambarish Tuly Dridh Vrat Ka Niyam Nahi,Harishchandra Si Na Dridhata Kasht Sahne Ki. [2]Moradhwaj Jaisa Mujhe Dharm Ka Bhi Prem Nahi,Shraddha Nahi Sur Si Prem-Path Gahne Ki. [3]Aradhana Na Aur Koi Kar Sakta Nath,Sadhana Ek Meri Vrindavan Rahne Ki. [4]- Dandi Swami Shri Hare Krishnanand Sarasvati ‘Hare Krishn’, Vrindavan Shatak (76)O Lord! I do not possess the strength like Dhruva to perform unwavering penance,Nor do I have the devotion like Prahlāda to chant Your holy name constantly. [1]I cannot uphold vows with the firmness of King Ambarīṣa,Nor do I have the endurance like Harishchandra to bear immense hardships. sanskrit_text: Reejhi Pare Chhavi Dhaam Par, Kari Naunchaavari Deh.Tab Tiy Sut Dhan Aadi Dain, Poochhai Ko Tujh Geh.- Shri Priyadas Ji, Rasik Mohini (20)When one becomes captivated by Shri Vrindavan Dham and surrenders to it, all worldly attachments—wife, children, wealth, and home seem utterly insignificant.

title: Ve Unki Dhare Mor Pakha Sir - Braj Ke Sawaiya
sanskrit_text: (Sawaiya)Ve Unki Dhare Mor Pakha Sir, Ve Unki Dhare Chandrika Pyari. [1]Ve Unki Dhare Peetpatti It, Ve Unki Sajein Sundar Saari. [2]Dekhat Hi Ban Aabe Chhata, Vrajchandrane Kunjan Aaya Samhari. [3]Vrishbhanulali Bani Nandalala, Bane Nandalala Vrishbhanudulari. [4]- Braj Ke SawaiyaShe wears His peacock-feathered crown, while He adorns Her crescent-shaped ornament upon His head. [1]She adorns Herself in His yellow garment, while He adorns Himself in Her exquisite sāṛī. [2]As Vraja Candra (the two moons of Braj) enter the groves, their divine glow illuminates the entire forest. [3]Today, Vṛṣabhanu's daughter (Śrī Rādhā) has become Nandalāla (Śrī Kṛṣṇa), and Nandalāla has become Vṛṣabhanu's beloved daughter. [4]

With pure bhava (emotions), see yourself as their Sahachari (intimate attendant) and experience the bliss of Nikunj Seva (service in their sacred grove).

title: Aaju Bani Ri Kunjeshwari Rani - Shri Govind Swami Ji Ki Vani
sanskrit_text: (Raag Kedaro)Aaju Bani Ri Kunjeshwari Rani.Charu Chikur Sithil Sagbagan, Vividh Kusum Beni Bani.Nain Surang Giridhar Rasmate, Kamal Kanjan Sobha Bilkhani.“Govind” Prabhu Kon Tu Nyain Bas Karati Dhani Dhani Ri,Vidhna Apun Chaturai Sakal Tomen Aani.- Shri Govind Swami, Shri Govind Swami Ji Ki VaniOh, today the queen of the groves (Kunjeshwari), Sri Radha has adorned herself beautifully! Her charming, curly locks flow loosely, decorated with various fragrant flowers woven into a braid. [1]Her reddish eyes, filled with love for Giridhar (Krishna), surpass the beauty of blooming lotuses and put the playful wagtail birds (khanjan) to shame. Sri Govind Swami says, O Radha! You have completely captivated Krishna’s heart! Blessed, truly blessed are you, for the Creator has poured all artistic brilliance and beauty within you! [2]

title: Bade Bhagya Basibo Brij Pabai - Shri Ramsharan Ji
sanskrit_text: Bade Bhagya Basibo Brij Pabai.Jaapai Karai Kripa Shri Radhe, Soi Taj Jag Yahan Aabai. [1]Hoy Puneet Mitai Mal Man Ke, Jab Raj Bhaal Lagabai.Sebai Sant Swarth Taji Apno, Sam Dam Niyam Nibhavai. [2]Anugat Chalai Tyag Hath Apno, Bhav Bandhan Kati Jabai.‘Ramsharan’ Kar Bas Biraj, Ghanshyam Sahaj Mil Jabai. [3]- Shri Ramsharan JiOnly by great fortune does one attain residence in Vraja Dham. Only those whom Shri Radha graces can renounce the material world and arrive here. [1]Their hearts are purified, and all impurities fade away when they lovingly apply the dust of Braj on their foreheads. Serving saints selflessly, practicing self-restraint, and following righteous conduct lead one to true devotion. [2]Walking the path of surrender, renouncing ego and obstinacy, severs the bondage of material existence. Sri Ramsharan says—By residing in Braj, one attains Shri Ghanshyam (Krishna) effortlessly. [3]

title: Shri Vrindavan Mahal Sukh Hai Sab Ras Ko Saar - Shri Roop Rasik Devacharya, Vishisht Doha (17)
sanskrit_text: Shri-Vrindavan Mahal Sukh, Hai Sab Ras Ko Saar.‘Rooprasik’ Jinko Mile, Tinpar Kripa Apaar.- Shri Roop Rasik Devacharya, Vishisht Doha (17)The divine nectar of Shri Vrindavan, the personal palace of Sri Shyama Shyam, is the essence of all nectars. title: Mohi Mati Rokai Ri Tu Eri Braj Naagari- Shri Narayan Swami, Braj Vihar, Sambhram-Manalila (11)
sanskrit_text: (Raag Jhinjhoti)Mohi Mati Rokai Ri Tu, Eri Braj Naagari.Roop Ki Nidhan Hai Tu, Gunan Ki Khan Hai Tu,Teri Sam Kaun Aaj, Tero Bado Bhaag Ri. [1]Kahai To Main Nrity Karoon, Bansuri Mein Raag Bharoon,Kanharo Kidaro Bhairon, Sorath Bihag Ri.Tu To Sada Upkaari, Hit Ki Karanhaari,Aaj Narayan Moson, Kyon Raakhai Tu Laag Ri. [2]- Shri Narayan Swami, Braj Vihar, Sambhram-Manalila (11)As Shri Krishna reaches the entrance of the kunja to pacify the sulking Shri Radha, a sakhi of Sri Radha stops Him. With folded hands and a yearning heart, Krishna pleads:O Braj Nagari, my dear sakhi, let me pass—do not stop me from beholding my Priyaji. You are an ocean of beauty and a treasury of divine virtues—who can compare to your fortune today? [1]Shall I dance if you command? Shall I please your heart with the melodies of my flute?Bhairav, Kanharo, Kedaro, Sorath, and Bihag—I shall play them all for you.You are ever merciful, ever kind—Then why, O sakhi, do you stand as an obstacle before me today? [2]

title: Kripa Saagari Naagari Veyi Pujavain Aash -  Shri Ananya Ali Ji Ki Vani, Shri Vrindavan Vaas Avastha (2.97)
sanskrit_text: Kripa Saagari Naagari, Veyi Pujavain Aash.Ihi Bal Veparwah Nit, Shri Vrindavan Vaas.- Shri Ananya Ali, Shri Ananya Ali Ji Ki Vani, Shri Vrindavan Vaas Avastha (2.97)Shri Radha, the fathomless ocean of mercy and sovereign queen of Vrindavan, is the only one I worship and surrender to, for She alone fulfills every longing of my heart. With firm faith in Her, I remain forever carefree and dwell ceaselessly in Shri Vrindavan Dham.

title: Vrindavan Chhadi Kahun Sukh Nahi - Shri Hita Gopal Das [Of Sewa Kunj], Nikunj Ras Vallari (67)
sanskrit_text: (Raag Hamir Tritaal)Vrindavan Chhadi Kahun Sukh Nahi.Sundar Yamuna Pritam Pyari, Pyari Kadaman Chhahin. [1]Vanshivat Sebakunj Pyaro, Pyari Charan Davahin.Chal Gayandin Kunjan Vichare, Diye Yugal Galbahin. [2]Veni Gunthe Pritam Pyari, Tan Ki Sudh-Budh Nahi.Nishidin Abto Shri Gopalhit, Pyari Ke Gun Gai. [3]- Shri Hita Gopal Das [Of Sewa Kunj], Nikunj Ras Vallari (67)There is no happiness anywhere upon leaving Vrindavan. The sacred Yamuna, the divine couple, Sri Priyatama Pyari (Radha Krishna), and the soothing shade of Kadamba trees overflow with divine love and beauty. [1]At the banks of Vanshivat, in the sacred groves of Sevakunj, beloved Krishna lovingly massages the lotus feet of Sri Radha. Like gracefully swaying intoxicated elephants, the divine couple roam within the kunjas of Vrindavan, their arms around each other in a tender embrace. [2]Lost in love-bliss, Sri Krishna gently braids Sri Radha’s hair, forgetting all bodily awareness. Shri Hit Gopal Das, immersed in Sri Radha’s nectarean pastimes, now sings the glories of Sri Pyariju (Sri Radha), day and night. [3]

title: Lalit Mohini Kripa Te Nirakhat Keli Vilas - Sri Thakur Das Ju Ki Vani, Saakhi (5)

title: Dhan Dhan Vrindavan Ke Baasi - Shri Shyamsakha Ji
sanskrit_text: Dhan Dhan Vrindavan Ke Baasi.Aathon Pahar Rahat Ya Braj Mein Radha Krishna Upasi. [1]In Ke Ghar Par Let Madhukari Vitarag Sannyasi.Yaaki Mahima Soi Jaane Dhrid Shraddha Biswasi. [2]Jaa Vrindavan Ki Raj Parisat Kati Hain Lakh Chaurasi."Shyamsakha” Vrindavan Rahiye Sahaj Mile Avinasi. [3]- Shri Shyamsakha JiBlessed, blessed are the residents of Vrindavan!For all eight quarters of the day, they remain immersed in the loving devotion of the divine couple Shri Radha Krishna. [1]Even renounced ascetics, detached from worldly desires, seek alms at their doorsteps.Only those with unwavering faith in the Lord can truly understand their divine glory. [2]Simply by touching the sacred dust of Vrindavan, countless cycles of birth and death (8.4 million life forms) are eradicated.Shri Shyam Sakha says—Reside in Vrindavan, for here, the eternal and imperishable divine treasure is easily attained. [3]

title: Hori Khelain Shyama Shyam - Shri Roop Sakhi Ji Ki Vani, Shringar Ras Ke Pad (808)
sanskrit_text: (Raag Ramkali)Hori Khelain Shyama-Shyam.Drig Rang Bhari Bhrikuti Pichkai Chali Mridu Musikaani Baam. [1]Bajat Taal Mridang Ang Sang Vrindavan Chhavi Dham.Roop Sakhi Nyochhavar Kino Kotin Rati Jut Kaam. [2]- Shri Roop Sakhi, Shri Roop Sakhi Ji Ki Vani, Shringar Ras Ke Pad (808)The divine couple, Sri Shyama Shyam revel in the joyous colors of Holi, their captivating eyes drenched in the hues of divine love. Their arched eyebrows, like poised water guns, release a shower of playful glances, adorned with enchanting smiles. [1]With each movement, the rhythmic beats of the mridang blend harmoniously, as Vrindavan glows in its most radiant form.  Sri Roop Sakhi, overwhelmed by the glimpses of the couple, offers countless Ratis and Kamadevas upon them. [2]

title: Mere Pyare Mohna Mere Manke Chor - Braj Ke Dohe
sanskrit_text: Mere Pyare Mohna, Mere Manke Chor.Tero Mukh Dekhe Bina, Deekhat Nahin Koi Aur.- Braj Ke DoheO, My beloved Mohan (Sri Krishn), the thief of my heart! Without beholding your face, my eyes see nothing else.

title: Phag Ki Bhir Abhiran Te Gahi - Shri Padmakar
sanskrit_text: (Savaiya)Phag Ki Bheer Abheeran Te Gahi, Govindai Lai Gayi Bheetar Gori. [1]Bhaay Kari Man Ki Padmakar, Upar Naay Abheer Ki Jhori. [2]Chheen Pitambar Kamar Te, Subida Dai Meed Kapolan Rori. [3]Nain Nachay Kahyo Muskayi, Lala! Phir Khelan Aiyo Hori. [4]- Shri PadmakarAmidst the bustling crowd of the Holī festival, fair-complexioned Śrī Rādhā playfully caught hold of Śrī Kṛṣṇa and pulled Him inside. [1]Then, following the delight of Her heart, She grabbed handfuls of abīra and gulala, showering them all over Śrī Kṛṣṇa. [2]Afterward, She mischievously snatched away His yellow garment and shawl, smearing fragrant red powder all over His cheeks. [3]With teasing glances and a playful smile, Śrī Rādhā lovingly taunted Him, saying—"O Lālā! Be sure to come again to play Holī!" [4]

title: Ur Bich Gokul Nayan Jal Mukh Shrivallabh Naam - Goswami Shri Harirai Ji, Vallabh Saakhi (54)
sanskrit_text: Ur Bich Gokul Nayan Jal, Mukh Shri Vallabh Naam.As Tadrishi Ke Sang Tein, Hot Sakal Sidh Kaam.- Goswami Shri Harirai Ji, Vallabh Saakhi (54)One who keeps Gokul in their heart, tears of devotion in their eyes, and the divine name of Shri Vallabh (Krishna) on their lips—such a devotee attains the fulfillment of all their desires effortlessly.

title: Rangan Rang Ho Ho Hori Hai - Shri Lakshmiram
sanskrit_text: (Sawaiya)Rangan Rang Ho Ho Hori Hai,Koou Bhalaou Burau Jini Mano.Manmohan Ke Man Mohan Koun,Shri Vrishabhanu Kishori Hai. [1]Hori Mein Kaha Kaha Nahi Kahiat,Yamain Kaha Kuch Chori Hai.Krishna Jeevan Lachhiram Ke Prabhu Saon,Jo Kahiye So Thori Hai. [2]- Shri Lakshmiram The festival of Holī is filled with vibrant colors—let no one perceive it as good or bad. The one who captivates even Manamohana's (Kṛṣṇa's) heart is none other than Śrī Vṛṣabhanu Kiśorī (Śrī Rādhā). [1]During Holī, words flow freely in playful exchange; there is no need for restraint in this joyous celebration. For Kṛṣṇa, who is the very life of Lakṣmīrāma, any praise we offer still falls short. [2]

title: Khelat Mohan Radha Gori - Shri Krishndas Adhikari Ji Ki Vani (976)
sanskrit_text: (Raag Kedaro)Khelat Mohan Radha Gori.Itahin Gopika Juri-Juri Aayi, Utahin Gwal Mandali Chaanchari Jori. [1]Piya Pyari Par Pyari Piya Par, Abir Gulal Ki Daarat Jhoori.‘Krisnadas’ Bali Jai Inni Par, Syama Syam Ki Jori. [2]- Shri Krishndas, Shri Krishndas Adhikari Ji Ki Vani (976)Shyamsundar joyfully plays Holi with the fair-complexioned Radhika.On one side, groups of Gopis eagerly gather, and on the other, the group of cowherd boys joined, dancing and playing in the rhythm of Chānchari. [1]Beloved Radha showers color upon Krishna, and Krishna lovingly showers color on Sri Radha in return, tossing handfuls of abir and gulal. Krishnadas says, “I surrender myself completely to this divine pair of Shyama and Shyam!” [2]

title: Prem Peer Ati Hi Bikala Kal Na Parat Din Rain - Shri Dayabai
sanskrit_text: Prem-Peer Ati Hee Bikala, Kal Na Parat Din Rain.Sundar Syam Sarup Bin, ‘Daya’ Lahat Nahin Chain.- Shri Dayabai (a disciple of Shri Charan Das Ji of the Shuk sect.)The agony of divine love has made me so restless that neither day nor night passes in peace. Without beholding the beautiful form of my beloved Shyamsundar, my heart finds no solace, even for a moment, says Dayabai.

title: Niko Lage Radha Var Pyaro - Shri Lalit Kishori, Abhilash Madhuri
sanskrit_text: Niko Lage Radha Var Pyaro.Mor Mukut Piyaro Patuka Hai, Lakuti Kar Matwaro. [1]Rokat Gail Chhail Albelu, Natvar Vesh Sanwaro.Lalit Kishori Mohan Rasiya, Jeevan Pran Hamaro. [2]- Shri Lalit Kishori, Abhilash MadhuriSri Radha’s beloved, Shri Krishna, is extremely dear to my heart. Adorned with a peacock feather crown, wearing yellow garments (Pitambar), holding a stick, with an enchanting swaying gait, He appears as the playful Lord. [1]That enchanting Lord, dressed in his ‘Natwar’ (divine dancer) attire, stands in the middle of the path, playfully blocking the way of the Gopis, engaging in loving pastimes. Shri Lalit Kishori Ji says—“That rasik (divine connoisseur of love) Mohan is the very essence of my life and soul.” [2]

title: Laadili Lalchat Hai Man Mero - Shri Saras Madhuri Ji
sanskrit_text: (Raga Sorath)Laadili Lalchat Hai Man Mero.Avichal Vaas Basoon Barsaane, Nit Nirakhoon Mukh Tero. [1]Seva Karoon Kripaanidhi Teri, Rahoo Charan Ke Nero.Saras Maadhuri Chhavi Avlokoon, Karon Aapno Chero. [2]- Shri Saras MadhuriMy heart longs for my beloved Ladili (Shri Radha). May I always reside in Barsana and behold Your divine face every day. [1]O ocean of mercy, let me serve You, always remaining close to Your lotus feet. Shri Saras Madhuri prays, “May I forever gaze upon Your sweet form—please accept me as Your servant anyhow.” [2]

title: Laaj Tajou Maskat Karo - Shri Hita Damodar Das, Nem Battisi (11)
sanskrit_text: Laaj Tajou Maskat Karo, Yau Nirvah Karaun.Shri Vrindavan Chhandi Ke, Anant Na Kit Hun Jaun.- Shri Hita Damodar Das, Nem Battisi (11)I will cast aside all hesitation and shame, embracing every hardship that comes my way. But I will never leave Vrindavan and go anywhere else.

title: Hum Basi Des Divane Ke - Shri Kishori Ali
sanskrit_text: (Raga Jhanjhoti)Hum Basi Des Divane Ke.Devi Devan Kaun Nahin Mane, Chakar Ajab Amane Ke.Rahen Hazur Liye Rukh Sanmukh, Khas Neelambar Bane Ke.Kau Kahai Vanaraj Raj Ke, Kau Kahai Barsane Ke.Radha Naam Bharose Gajen, Bas Nahin Raja Rane Ke.Ved Lok Ki Kan Na Manen, Janen Jas Umandane Ke.“Kishori” Ju Ke Hvai Kain Phir Nahin, Aur Na Hath Bikane Ke.- Shri Kishori AliWe belong to the land of those who are mad in love of Sri Radha. [1]We do not acknowledge other gods or goddesses, for we are the servants of the most divine and sovereign Swamini (Shri Radha).We remain ever-present before Her, holding Her favor in our hearts and remain engaged in the personal service of the one adorned in blue garments (Shri Radha). [2]Some say we belong to Vrindavan, the king of forests, while others claim we are from Barsana. But we live solely by the power of Shri Radha’s holy name, and never surrender to any other king or queen, for our one and only sovereign is Shri Radha Herself. [3]We do not follow the customs of society, nor do we entangle ourselves in the rules and regulations of the Vedas, for we remain ever intoxicated in lovingly chanting the glories of Sri Radha. Shri Kishori Ali says—“Now that we have surrendered at Shri Radha’s lotus feet, we cannot belong to anyone else. Our everything, our very existence, belongs only to Shri Radha.” [4]

title: Nain Bain Radha Gahe Rahe Preeti Ke Taari - Shri Vanshi Ali, Madhuriya Shat (102.2)
sanskrit_text: Nain Bain Radha Gahe, Rahe Preeti Ke Taari.Radha Ke Sakhi Vadan Kajhi, Rom Rom Phulwari.- Shri Vanshi Ali, Madhuriya Shat (102.2)Shri Radha, the supreme enchantress, has captured the eyes and voices of the sakhis, binding them completely under the spell of Her love. Each glance upon Her sweet form now fills their hearts with bliss, as if a garden of fragrant blossoms has bloomed in every pore of their being.

title: Nirjanani Nagari Kalbaini Sukumari - Shri Harivyas Devacharya, Mahavani, Sahaj Sukh (75)
sanskrit_text: (Doha)Nirjanani Nagari, Kalbaini Sukumari.Shrihari Pyari Nit Hiye, Basau Sada Sukhkari.(Pad)Jai Jai Priya Pran-Piya Pyari.Jai Jai Roop Ujari Radhe, Ati Sundar Sukumari.Jai Jai Nirjanani Nagari, Kalbaini Kamala Ri.Jai Jai Shriharipriya Hiye, Nit Basau Sada Sukhkari.- Shri Harivyas Devacharya, Mahavani, Sahaj Sukh (75)Seeing Shri Lal Ji’s deep yearning and restlessness, Shri Hari Priya Sakhi Ji humbly prays to Shri Priya Ji (Shri Radha) -(Doha)O graceful lotus-eyed Nagariji (Shri Radha)! O gentle and soft-spoken Sukumariji! You are the dearest beloved of Shri Hari. Therefore, please embrace Him and grant Him supreme bliss.(Pad)O Priyaju! You are dearer to beloved Lalji than His life—glory to You!O, the most resplendent Sri Radhaju, embodiment of supreme beauty—glory to You! [1]O Nagariji, with lotus-like eyes! O sweet-speaking Padmaniji—glory to You!You are the beloved of Sri Hari. May you forever reside in your beloved’s heart, showering love-bliss. [2]

title: Guru Raakhai Phoutau Karvaa - Shri Lalitmohini Dev Ju Ki Vani (35)
sanskrit_text: Guru Raakhai Phoutau Karvaa, Lagaavai Raj.Chela Rangai Baanki, Banaavai Saj.- Shri Lalitmohini Dev, Shri Lalitmohini Dev Ju Ki Vani (35)What a strange irony it is that the Rasika Gurus lead an extremely simple life—keeping only a broken earthen pot, adorning themselves with the sacred dust of Shri Dham Vrindavan, and remaining immersed in pure, selfless devotion. Meanwhile, the so-called disciples consider the dust of Vrindavan insignificant, indulge in colorful attire, and remain engrossed in external decoration and display.

title: Khelat Phag Suhaag Bhari Anuraag Bhari - Shri Hita Vrindavan Das
sanskrit_text: (Raag Lalit)Khelat Phag Suhaag Bhari Anuraag Bhari Badbhaagi Piya Soon. [1]Baal Gulal Lai Laal Pai Daarat, Nihal Hoy Laal Lagaav Hiyaa Soon. [2]Kesar Ki Pichkaari Bharein Piya, Chhirakhin Chheent Sneh Jiyaa Soon. [3]‘Vrindavan’ Dampati Chhavi Nirakhat, Kaun Kare Rati Kaam Maya Soon. [4]- Shri Hita Vrindavan DasThe supremely fortunate Shri Radha, filled with divine love and bliss, joyfully plays Holi with her beloved Shri Krishna. [1]She takes handfuls of crimson gulal and sprinkles it upon Shri Krishna, while He, overwhelmed with bliss, lovingly embraces her. [2]Shri Krishna fills His pichkari (water gun) with saffron-colored water and playfully sprinkles it upon Radha with immense tenderness. [3]Shri Hit Vrindavan Das Ji says—“Upon witnessing the divine Holi pastimes of the beloved couple, who could still be drawn to the passions of Kamadeva (Cupid) and His consort Rati?” [4]

title: Na Vishaya Bhogo Bhaagyam  - Shri Vagish Shastri Ji, Shri Radha Saptashati (5.62)
sanskrit_text: Na Vishaya Bhogo Bhaagyam Keertirvaa Vistṛitaa Loke.Brahmendradya-Abhilashitam Bhaagyam Vrindaavane Vaasah.- Shri Vagish Shastri Ji, Shri Radha Saptashati (5.62)Neither an abundance of material wealth nor worldly fame brings true fortune. title: Priya Shyam Roop Rang Maati - Shri Thakurdas Ji
sanskrit_text: Priya Shyam Roop Rang Maati.Ang Ang Anuraag Badhao Ati, Sobha Kahi Na Jaati. [1]Tan Sau Tan Man Sau Man Milwat, Chhaati Sau Lagaai Chhaati.Thakur Sakhi Ya Chhabi Par Wari, Baar Baar Suukh Paati. [2]- Shri Thakur Das, Sri Thakur Das Ju Ki Vani, Pad (1)The divine couple, Shri Radha Krishna, are completely immersed in each other’s unparalleled beauty and sweetness. Every limb of their divine bodies overflows with ever-increasing love, a beauty beyond description. [1]They embrace each other so intimately, uniting their bodies, minds and souls, as if merging into one. Shri Thakur Sakhi repeatedly sacrifices Herself to these glimpses, immersed in the ecstasy of divine love-bliss. [2]

title: Namo Namo Shriharidas Vrindavipin - Shri Agradas Ji (Spiritual master of Nabha ji)
sanskrit_text: (Sawaiya)Namo Namo Shriharidas VrindavipinVas Var Pran Sarvas Bankebihari. [1]Shyama Shyama Jugala Roopa Madhurya KeRasik Rijhwar Prem Avatari. [2]Param Vairag-Nidhi Basat NidhivanSada Bhavana Leen Supraveen Bhari. [3]Kamana Kalpataru Sakal Santaapahru‘Agradas’ Ali Kalyankari. [4]- Shri Agradas Ji (Spiritual master of Nabha Ji)Salutations, salutations to Svāmī Śrī Haridāsa, the rasika saint forever residing in Vṛndāvana,Whose very life and breath are entirely dedicated to Śrī Bāṅke Bihārī. [1]He is the crown jewel among Rasikas, those immersed in the sweetness of the divine couple, Śrī Śyāmā-Śyāma's eternal love-filled plays. In truth, He is the very embodiment of divine love. [2]With supreme renunciation, He resides eternally in Nidhivana, Vṛndāvana,Always absorbed in devotion and ever-attentive in the loving service of the divine couple. [3]Like a wish-fulfilling tree, He removes all kinds of sorrows.Śrī Agradāsa says, "Svāmī Śrī Haridāsa Jī is supremely benevolent and auspicious to those who come to Him." [4]

title: Prabhuta Hi Ko Sab Maro Prabhu Ko Marai Na Koy - Shri Malook Das
sanskrit_text: Prabhuta Hi Ko Sab Maro, Prabhu Ko Marai Na Koy.Jo Koi Prabhu Ko Marai, To Prabhuta Dasi Hoy.- Shri Malook DasEveryone desires lordship, but none desires the Lord Himself. If one surrenders to the Lord, then even lordship becomes a servant.

title: Rasa Lai To Dwaar Paryo Rahiyo - Sri Purushottam Ji
sanskrit_text: Rasa Lai To Dwaar Paryo Rahiyo.Jo Tu Rasiya Ras Ko Bhukho, Maar Dhaari Sab Ki Sahiyo. [1]Jaiyo Na Kahun In Dwaarana Te, Lali Charanana Ko Sukh Paiyo.Purushottam Prabhu Ki Chhavi Nirakhai, Prem Sudha Ko Ras Chakiyo. [2]- Sri Purushottam JiIf you truly desire the nectar of divine love, then remain steadfast at Her doorway. If you are indeed a true rasika (one who relishes divine love), then endure all hardships and afflictions with patience, for the reward (of rasa) is unparalleled. title: Sab Braj Gopin Ke Basi Baat Yehai Man Aan - Shri Brajavasidas, Braj Vilas
sanskrit_text: Sab Braj Gopin Ke Basi, Baat Yehai Man Aan.Hari-Radha Dou Milain, Nishi Vaasar Yeh Dhyaan.- Shri Brajavasidas, Braj VilasFor all the Gopis of Braj, only one thought fills their hearts—‘May Hari (Shri Krishna) and Radha unite, and may this be our constant meditation, day and night.’

title: Nit Nit Hori Braj Mein Rahau - Shri Bhartendu Harishchandra, Bhartendu Granthawali, Holi (79)
sanskrit_text: Nit Nit Hori Braj Mein Rahau.Viharat Hari-Sang Braj-Jubatigan, Sada Anand Lahau.Phulit Phalit Rahau Vrindavan, Madhup Krishna-Gun Kahau.‘Harichand’ Nit Saras Sudhamay, Prem-Pravah Chahau.- Shri Bhartendu Harishchandra, Bhartendu Granthawali, Holi (79)The festival of Holi is eternally celebrated in Braj, where Shri Hari joyfully plays with the young maidens of Braj, and they forever revel in divine bliss. [1]Eternal Sri Dham Vrindavan remains ever-blooming and fruitful, where Rasikas, like buzzing bumblebees, hum the glories of Shri Krishna. Shri Harichand prays—‘May my heart forever yearn for the ever-flowing, nectar-filled stream of divine love.’ [2]

title: Vrindavan Ki Yaad Jo Aawat Hai - Shri Ramray, Geet Govind Braj Bhasha, Doha (85)
sanskrit_text: Vrindavan Ki Yaad Jo, Aavat Hai Man Maahi.Tabhi Radha Naagri, Pati Sang Taahi Saranhi.- Shri Ramray, Geet Govind Braj Bhasha, Doha (85)Whoever remembers Vrindavan, at that very moment, Shri Radha, along with her beloved Shri Krishna, mercifully accepts and blesses them.

title: Payan Paayali Jagmag Jyoti - Shri Albeli Ali, Samay Prabandh (109)
sanskrit_text: Payan Paayali Jagmag Jyoti.Nav Navratan Deep Se Sohain, Tora Badide Moti. [1]Ta Par Nupur Subhag Birajen, Keli Kala Udyoti.Albeli Piya Hiy Ko Gahino, Naval Prem Ras Soti. [2]- Shri Albeli Ali, Samay Prabandh (109)The divine anklets of Sri Radha shine with unparalleled brilliance, adorned with nine precious gems that sparkle like radiant lamps. Strung together with large, lustrous pearls, they shimmer with divine beauty. [1]Her nūpura (ankle bells), ringing with enchanting melodies, illuminates the essence of 'Keli Kala' (playful pastimes). Sri Albeli Ali says that these anklets are the most treasured adornment of Her beloved’s heart, ceaselessly showering an eternal stream of ever-fresh divine love. [2]

title: Jog Yagya Tap Nem Kari Bhaje Nahin Govind - Shri Guruchauna Ji Maharaj
sanskrit_text: Jog Yagya Tap Nem Kari, Bhajai Nahin Govinda,‘Chhona’ Hari Ke Naam Bin, Chhoote Nahin Bhav Fanda.- Shri Guruchauna Ji MaharajOne may practice yoga, perform yajñas (sacrificial rituals), engage in penance, and follow strict vows, but without true devotion to Govinda (Sri Krishna) and the continuous chanting of God’s name, no one can be freed from the bondage of worldly existence.

title: Phoole Hain Palaas Aas Paas - Shri Lal Balbir Ji, Braj Binod, Shadritu Shatak, Basant Ritu (26)
sanskrit_text: (Kavitta)Phoole Hain Palaas Aas Paas Ban Baagan Mein,Madhur Madhur Ter Kokoila Lagai Hai. [1]Gunjat Madhur Punj Kunj Kunjan Mein,Sheetal Sugandh Mand Pavan Suhai Hai. [2]‘Lal Balveer’ Bas Baalam Videsh Rahe,Ko Kare Sahay Peer Main Ko Savai Hai. [3]Pathik Praveen Pyare Itni Kripa Karike,Kahiyo Jaay Kant Soun Basant Ritu Aai Hai. [4]- Shri Lal Balbir Ji, Braj Binod, Shadritu Shatak, Basant Ritu (26)The Pālāś trees have blossomed across the forests and gardens, and the cuckoo sings a sweet melody. [1]The humming of bees fills the bowers, and the gentle, fragrant breeze brings joy. [2]Lāl Balveer says, “If the beloved is far away in a distant land, who will ease this sorrow, as my pain only grows?” [3]O dear traveler, have mercy and convey this message; tell my beloved Śyāmasundara that the season of spring has arrived!. [4]

title: Guna Mandira Sundara Yugala - Shri Narayan Swami, Anurag Ras (184)
sanskrit_text: Guna Mandira Sundara Yugala, Mangala Modanidhan.Narayana Nija Charana Rati, Yaha Dijaim Varadan.- Shri Narayan Swami, Anurag Ras (184)The divine couple, Sri Radha Krishna, is the temple of virtues and the source of auspiciousness and happiness. Shri Narayan Swami humbly prays, “O gracious ones, grant me the priceless boon of love at your lotus feet.”

title: Khelat Basant Hori Naval Chabili Jori -  Shri Dhruvdas, Bayalees Leela, Shringar Shat (3.21)
sanskrit_text: (Kavitt)Khelat Basant Hori Naval Chabili Jori,Udat Gulal Anurag Kau Surang Ree. [1]Mridu Muskani Ur Phool Aayi Phool Bhaye,Haav-Bhaav Saundhe Bhinje Sohain Ang-Ang Ree. [2]Nainan Ki Chitvani Chirakani Prem-Neer,Seenchat Hain Piya-Hiya Bhari Ras-Rang Ree. [3]‘Hit Dhruv’ Bhinje Sukh Baridh Vilas Haans,Soi Sukh Dekhain Sakhi Dinahin Abhang Ree. [4]- Shri Dhruvdas, Bayalees Leela, Shringar Shat (3.21)The ever‑beautiful divine couple, Śrī Rādhā and Śrī Kṛṣṇa, celebrate the arrival of Vasant (Spring), the king of seasons, by joyfully inaugurating Holi, playfully scattering the gulālā of divine love. [1]Their gentle smiles and joyful hearts shower flower‑like bliss, filling the air with divine fragrance; Their limbs, soaked in the essence of love, appear even more enchanting. [2]Śrī Rādhā’s love‑filled glances become streams of colored nectar, gently sprinkling upon Kṛṣṇa’s heart, immersing Him in divine love. [3]Śrī Hit Dhruvadās Jī says, “In this ocean of joy and playful exchanges, the divine couple remains forever intoxicated in rasa (divine nectar), while the sakhīs relish this bliss eternally”. [4]

title: Hari Heera Guru Jauhari - Shri Hariram Vyas, Vyas Vani, Siddhant Ki Saakhi (23)
sanskrit_text: Hari Heera Guru Jauhari, Vyasa Hi Diyo Bataai.Tan Man Anand Sukh Mile, Naam Let Dukh Jaai.- Shri Hariram Vyas, Vyas Vani, Siddhant Ki Saakhi (23)Shri Hariram Vyas says, “Hari is the divine jewel, and the Guru is the jeweler. By chanting the Lord’s name, one attains bliss in both body and mind.”

title: Sajani Nav Nikunja Drum Phule - Shri Vitthal Vipul Dev Ju Ki Vani (14)
sanskrit_text: (Raag Basant)Sajani Nav Nikunja Drum Phule,Ali-Kul-Sankul Karat Kulaahal,Saurabh Manmath Mule.Harashi Hindoren Rasik Raasi Var,Jugal Parspar Jhule.Shri Bithal Vipul Vinod Dekhi Nabha,Dev Vimaanani Bhule.- Shri Vitthal Vipul Dev Ji, Shri Vitthal Vipul Dev Ju Ki Vani (14)While describing the unparalleled sweetness of Vasant (spring), one sakhi says to another—O sakhi! In this Vasant season, the trees and vines have fully blossomed, filling the entire forest with the intoxicating fragrance of flowers.Swarms of bees hum joyfully, their melodious buzzing weaving a song of love, awakening Cupid’s playful presence. [1]In this enchanting season, the king of rasikas, Shri Bihari (Shri Krishna), and Shri Biharini (Shri Radha) sway gently in divine union upon a swing, immersed in the ecstasy of love.The radiant beauty of this divine scene in Shri Vrindavan is so mesmerizing that even the celestial gods, beholding this scene, lose awareness of their own bodies, becoming utterly absorbed in divine love-bliss. [2]

title: Hare Krishna Hi Krishna Ka Kirtan Mein - Dandi Swami Shri Hare Krishnanand Sarasvati
sanskrit_text: (Sawaiya)Hare Krishna Hi Krishna Ka Kirtan Mein, Machata Rahe Ghanghor Yahan. [1]Sunlo Sunlo Yamunajal Mein, Murli Dhvani Ka Vah Shor Yahan. [2]Taru Radhe Hi Radhe Pukaar Rahe, Khinchata Man Hai Barjor Yahan. [3]Kar Prem Koi Lakh Le Usko, Rehta Ab Bhi Chitchor Yahan. [4]- Dandi Swami Shri Hare Krishnanand Sarasvati ‘Hare Krishn’In the kīrtana of Lord Kṛṣṇa, an intense devotional atmosphere resounds here. [1]Listen, listen to the sacred waters of Yamunā, where the melody of Śrī Kṛṣṇa's flute forever echoes. [2]Even the trees keep calling out 'Rādhe Rādhe', and the heart gets drawn strongly to this place due to that call. [3]Whoever longs for Śrī Kṛṣṇa's darśana with pure love shall still find the Heart-Stealer here, in this nectar-filled land of Vṛndāvana. [4]

title: Shri Vanraj Vilasini Mriduhasini Sukh Punj - Braj Ke Dohe
sanskrit_text: Shri Vanraj Vilasini, Mriduhasini Sukh Punj,Shri Krishna Vallabha Radhike, Jai Jai Sevakunj.- Braj Ke DoheO Shri Radhike! title: Shri Radha Charan Pradhan - Shri Nabhadas, Bhaktamala (90)
sanskrit_text: (Chhapay)Shri Radha Charan Pradhan Hriday Ati Sudridh Upasi,Kunj Keli Dampati Tahan Ki Karat Khawasi. [1]Sarvasu Mahaprasad Prasiddh Take Adhikari,Vidhi Nishedh Nahi Das Ananya Utkat Vratdhari. [2]Shri Vyas Suvan Path Anusarai Soi Bhalai Pehichanihai,Shri Harivansh Gusain Bhajan Ki Reeti Sukrit Kou Janihai. [3]- Shri Nabhadas, Bhaktamala (90)Shri Nabha Das Ji describes the glory of Shri Hit Harivansh Mahaprabhu:Shri Harivansh Ji, a Rasik Acharya, is exclusively devoted to the lotus feet of Shri Radha. His entire devotion is centered upon the lotus feet of Shri Radha. He never wavers, nor does he seek anything beyond serving the divine feet of Swamini Shri Radha. Eternally, he resides and serves in the sacred Nikunj bowers, where the divine couple engages in eternal love plays. [1]His faith in the Mahaprasad (sacred remnants) of Shri Radha was unshakable, and he alone was truly deserving of it. For him, scriptural injunctions and prohibitions held no significance, as his sole dharma was to love and serve Shri Radha with utmost affection—this was his eternal vow. [2]The divine stature of Shri Harivansh Ji can only be understood by one who walks the path of exclusive devotion to Shri Radha’s lotus feet. Shri Nabha Das Ji declares that only a supremely fortunate devotee can comprehend the confidential depth and bhajan tradition of Shri Harivansh Goswami’s devotion. [3]

title: Ve Jamuna Ve Sakha Hamare - Shri Surdas, Sura Sagara (4892)
sanskrit_text: Ve Jamuna, Ve Sakha Hamaare, Nit Nav Keli Vihaari.Vrindavan Ki Gulm-Lata Hain, Man-Madhukar Ko Pyaari.- Shri Surdas, Sura Sagara (4892)Shri Krishna says to Satyabhama—“I solemnly swear that the sacred Yamuna, my beloved Brajvasi friends, my ever-new playful pastimes with the sakhis, and the flowers and vines of Vrindavan are all supremely dear to the bee of my heart.”

title: Saghan Van Chhayo Praphullit Drumveli - Goswami Shri Harirai Ji
sanskrit_text: (Raga Bhairav)Saghan Van Chhayo Praphullit Drumveli,Bhayo Hulas Braj Jan Man. [1]Thor Thor Kokil Kal Kujat,Gunjar Madhup Gan. [2]Bhayo Prakat Aaj Rituraj,Vaas Kiyo Suniyat Vrindavan. [3]Rasik Preetam Piy So Ras Vilso,Aani Arpo Sakhi Tan Man Dhan. [4]- Goswami Shri Harirai JiSeeing the forest adorned with dense trees and blooming vines, the hearts of the people of Braj are filled with joy. [1]Everywhere, cuckoos sing their sweet melodies, and swarms of bees hum in harmony. [2]Today, the king of seasons, spring, has fully blossomed, gracing the sacred land of Vrindavan with its divine presence. [3]Preetam Lord Krishna engages in love-play with His beloved Radha. O Sakhi, surrender your body, mind, and wealth to the divine couple. [4]

title: Ankhiya Roopsudha Mad Matin - Shri Lalit Madhuri
sanskrit_text: (Raag Khammach)Ankhiya Roopsudha Mad Matin.Bin Dekhe Vah Yugal Sughar Chhavi, Bahu Atur Akulatin. [1]Vani Pari Rati Charan Kamal Ki, Av Kaise Sachupati.Lalit Madhuri Darsan Dijai, Vahiko Lalasatin. [2]- Shri Lalit MadhuriMy eyes are intoxicated by the nectar of the divine beauty of the Divine Couple, Shri Shyama-Shyam. Without beholding them, they remain restless and agitated. [1]Naturally bound in eternal love, they remain fixed at the lotus feet of the Divine Couple, finding no solace in anything else. Sri Lalit Madhuri says, “Grant me Your divine darshan, for that alone is my deepest longing.” [2]

title: Prem Diwane Jo Bhay Kahe Bahkte Nain - Sri Sahjobai
sanskrit_text: Prem Divane Jo Bhaye, Kahain Bahakte Bain.Sahjo Mukh Hansi Chhute, Kabahu Tapkai Nain.- Sri SahjobaiThose intoxicated with the divine love of God may appear strange and speak in ways that seem bewildering. One moment, they shed tears in remembrance of the Lord; the next, they burst into blissful laughter.

title: Priya Main To Hoon Cherin Ki Cheri - Shri Roop Madhuri Ji Ki Vani, Padavali (125)
sanskrit_text: (Raag Kanhara or Bilaval)Priya Main To Hoon Cherin Ki Cheri.Ab To Karun Sanbhar Ladili, Bahutak Bhai Aberi. [1]Nishidin Virah Satavat Moko, Sudhi Ab Levo Saberi.De Darshan Man Mohani Shyama, Tanak Na Kije Deri. [2]Tum Bin Mere Aur Na Koi, Sakal Thaur Ho Heri.“Roopmadhuri” ‘Saras’ Piyari, Tumhein Laaj Hai Meri. [3]- Shri Roop Madhuri, Shri Roop Madhuri Ji Ki Vani, Padavali (125)O Priyaji (Sri Radha), I am the servant of your servants. Now, please take care of me, O Ladili, for it has already been delayed too long. [1]Day and night, the fire of separation torments me; please think about me now. O enchanting Shyama Ju (Radha), kindly grant me your divine darshan without further delay. [2]Without you, I have no one; I have searched everywhere, yet found no one to call my own. Sri Roop Madhuri says, ‘O beloved Swamini of Saras Madhuriji! My honor rests in your hands.’ [3]

title: Yah Ati Lagati Hai Ab Niko - Shri Roop Rasik Devacharya
sanskrit_text: (Rag Basant)Yah Ati Lagati Hai Ab Neeko Kant-Kamini Kau Basant. [1]Arasi Parasi Biharo Bali Esehi Jahi Dekhi Dukh Nasant. [2]Sahaj Saunj Sukhdayak Sab Din Dampati-Duti Ju Lasant. [3]‘Rooprasik’ Jan Ke Man Kau, Mahaghanras Ban Barasanta. [4]- Shri Roop Rasik DevacharyaThis divine season of Vasant (spring), now graced by the presence of the divine couple, Shri Radha-Krishna, is utterly enchanting, filling the heart with immense joy. [1]Seeing them performing love-play in each other’s embrace, all sorrows naturally fade away. [2]They are the eternal source of supreme bliss, and the radiance of their divine limbs shines so brilliantly that all else fades in comparison. [3]Shri Roop Rasik Devacharya Ji says that Yugal Sarkar immerses the hearts of their devotees completely in the ocean of transcendental nectar. [4]

title: Drishti Pari Sanket Main Jab Te Bhanukumari - Shri Brajnidhi Granthawali, Preeti Lata (59)
sanskrit_text: Drishti Pari Sanket Main, Jab Ten Bhanu-Kumari.Barsane Ki Or Kau, Tab Ten Rahe Nihari.- Shri Brajnidhi Ji, Shri Brajnidhi Granthawali, Preeti Lata (59)Ever since Shri Krishna first laid eyes on Shri Radha in Sanket Gram (situated between Barsana and Nandgaon), His gaze has remained fixed upon Barsana. His heart, lost in Radha’s beauty, yearns for the bliss of beholding Her again.

title: Chali Chalihi Vrindavan Vasant Aayo -  Shri Hariram Vyas, Vyas Vani, Uttarardh (326)
sanskrit_text: (Raag Vasant)Chali Chalihi Vrindavan Vasant Aayo.Jhoolat Phoolani Ke Jhanvara, Marut Makarand Udayo. [1]Madhukar Kokil Keer Keki Mili, Kolahal Upjayo.Naachat Shyam Bajavat Gavat, Radha Raag Jamayo. [2]Choba Chandan Booka Vandan, Laal Gulaal Udayo.Vyas Swamini Ki Chhavi Nirkhat, Rom Rom Sachu Payo. [3]- Shri Hariram Vyas, Vyas Vani, Uttarardh (326)Come, let us go! Spring has arrived in Vrindavan. Clusters of blooming flowers sway gracefully, while the gentle breeze spreads their sweet fragrance far and wide. [1]Bees, cuckoos, parrots, and peacocks sing together in joyous celebration. Shyam (Krishna) dances, and plays His flute, while Radha enchants all with Her melodious raga. [2]Fragrant sandalwood, scented powders, and offerings of colors fill the sky with a burst of red gulal. Shri Hariram Vyas says, ‘Beholding the divine beauty of my Swamini, Shri Radha, every pore of my being is immersed in bliss.’ [3]

title: Bhajan Kundaliya Mein Rahau - Shri Hita Dhruvdas, Bayalis Leela, Bhajan Kundaliyan (22)
sanskrit_text: Bhajan Kundaliya Mein Rahau, Pag Baahir Jini Dehu.Ekai Jugal-Kisor Saun, Kari Dhruv Sahaj Sanehu.- Shri Hita Dhruvdas, Bayalis Leela, Bhajan Kundaliyan (22)Shri Dhruvdas instructs, O devotees! Remain firmly within the sacred circle of devotion, never allowing even a single step beyond its boundary. With unwavering faith, cultivate spontaneous and exclusive love for the divine couple, Shri Radha Krishna.

title: Agam Rituraj Ka Samaj-Saaj Vrindavan - Shri Sharan Bihari Goswamiji
sanskrit_text: (Kavitt)Agam Rituraj Ka Samaj-Saaj Vrindavan,Naach Rahi Sobha Har Upvan-Van-Kyari Ki. [1]Arunim Nav Paat-Paat, Gaat Gaat Gamak Uthi,Phoolan Sehnai Baji Madhup Mahari Ki. [2]Phoolan Ki Sej Pe Biraje Piy-Pyari, Nyari,Sakhiyan Ki Chaav-Bhari Bheer Bhaav-Bhari Ki. [3]Haridasi Phool Bhare Phool Soun Vasant Gaave,Vasant Ki Bahar Mein, Bahar Hai Bihari Ki. [4]- Shri Sharan Bihari GoswamijiWith the grand arrival of the king of seasons, spring, Vṛndāvan is adorned in splendor, dancing in joy, filling every grove and garden with its beauty. [1]The tender new leaves, glowing with a red hue, sway gracefully, while the buzzing bees play the śahanāī (wind instrument), announcing the festival of blossoms. [2]Upon a bed of soft blossoms, the divine couple, Priyā Priyatam, sit in divine resplendence, surrounded by a gathering of lovely sakhīs, filled with love and joyous enthusiasm. [3]Śrī Haridāsī Sākhī, utterly absorbed in love, sings songs of Basaṃta, carrying fragrant blooms, for in this festival of spring, the true glory is that of Śrī Banke Bihārījī. [4]

title: Jaaki Mayavash Biranchi Shiv - Braj Ke Dohe
sanskrit_text: Jaaki Mayavash Biranchi Shiv, Naachat Paar Na Paayo.Kartal Taal Bajay Taahi, Yuvtin Naach Nachayo.- Braj Ke DoheEven Brahma and Shiva, enchanted by the divine Maya of Bhagwan Shri Krishna, dance at His command yet fail to comprehend His true essence. Such Shri Krishna dances to the rhythmic claps of the maidens of Braj, bound by the pure love of their hearts.

title: Phoolyo Ri Saghan Van Tame - Shri Surdas, Sura Sagara
sanskrit_text: (Rag Malkos)Phoolyo Ri Saghan Van Tame Karat Ri Kokila Gaan. [1]Chal Ri Vrishbhan Nandini Chhadi Kathin Man Maan. [2]Nav Rituraj Aayo Ri Nairai Mili Kije Madhu Paan. [3]Soordas Piy Ko Rijhaiye Gai Sunai Meethi Taan. [4]- Shri Surdas, Sura SagaraO Pyari Ju! Behold how the dense bowers of Vrindavan are adorned with blooming flowers, spreading unparalleled beauty. The cuckoo sings sweet melodies among these vines as if whispering messages of love. [1]O charming daughter of King Vrishabhanu, Shri Radhe! Please set aside your sulk and come quickly. Your beloved Shyamsundar eagerly awaits you. [2]The glorious king of seasons, Basant, has arrived in all its splendor—why delay any longer? Unite with Shyamsundar, immerse yourself in the nectar of divine love, and revel in boundless bliss. [3]Shri Surdas Ji says, “Please your beloved Shri Krishna with your sweet melodies, so that He is irresistibly drawn to you, making this union even more enchanting.” [4]

[3]Surdas Piy Ko Rijhaiye Gai Sunai Mithi Tan. [4]- Shri Surdas, Sura SagaraO Pyari Ju! Behold how the dense bowers of Vrindavan are adorned with bluming flowers, spreading unparalleled beauty. title: Ati Tondik Ati Chikniyan - Shri Biharin Dev Ji Ki Vani, Siddhant Ki Saakhi (139)
sanskrit_text: Ati Tondik Ati Chikniyan, Adhik Chatur Itarai.Kitahi Vibhau Kit Thakurai, Juthani Kaun Lalachai.- Shri Biharin Dev Ji, Shri Biharin Dev Ji Ki Vani, Siddhant Ki Saakhi (139)Shri Krishna, in Braj, is naturally adorned with grandeur, elegance, and supreme splendor, filled with divine majesty. However, in the secluded bowers of Nikunj, as Kunja Bihari, He cares neither for His grandeur nor His lordly status. There, He remains surrendered at the lotus feet of Shri Priya Ji (Shri Radha), eagerly yearning for Her sacred prasad remnants.

title: Yeho Swamini Gajgamini Manbhamini - Shri Lalit Kishori, Abhilash Madhuri, Vinay (84)
sanskrit_text: (Raag Paraj)Yeho Swamini Gajgamini Manbhamini, Rasiya Lal Tiharo. [1]Karunadith Neeth Avaloko, Deen Dasa Meri Nirwaro. [2]Lalit Kishori Shrivan Vithin, Renu Banay Sees Pag Dharo. [3]Tarasat Hai Braj Dekhan Ko, Drig Yate Dukh Aur Kah Bharo. [4]- Shri Lalit Kishori, Abhilash Madhuri, Vinay (84)O my Swamini (Sri Radha), O graceful elephant-gaited, O enchantress of hearts, beloved Rasika Lal, Shri Krishna, belongs solely to you and follows only your instructions. [1]Please cast your merciful glance upon me and relieve me of my sorrowful state. [2]O Lalit Kishori (ever-youthful) Shri Radha! Please make me the dust of Shri Vrindavan’s pathways and bless me by placing your lotus feet upon my head. [3]My eyes long to behold the beauty of Braj—what greater sorrow could there be than this painful separation? [4]

title: Nain Dalali Chauhate Mana Manik Piy Haath - Shri Raskhan, Raskhan Ratnavali
sanskrit_text: Nain Dalalin Chauhaten, Man Manik Piy Haath.Raskhan Dhol Bajaike, Bechyo Hiy Jiy Saath.- Shri Raskhan, Raskhan RatnavaliA gopi says, “These eyes, acting as merchants, have sold my precious, jewel-like heart to Lord Shri Krishna. Now, Krishna has taken full possession of my very being. In this way, I have openly and publicly surrendered my mind and life to Him, announcing it with a drum beat.”

title: Biharin De Vrindavan Vaas - Shri Saras Madhuri Ji
sanskrit_text: (Raag Kanhara)Biharin De Vrindavan Vaas.Kunwari Kishori Swamini Mori, Vinay Suno Sukharas. [1]Seva Karun Kamal Pad Pyari, Man Mein Yeh Abhilas.Hazir Rahun Hajoor Hamesha, Nirkhun Raas Vilas. [2]Ati Kripal Karuna Ki Murti, Mohe Raabari Aas.Saras Madhuri Sharan Tihari, Devo Nikunj Nivas. [3]- Shri Saras MadhuriO Biharini (Shri Radha), grant me residence in Vrindavan. O ever-youthful, my beloved Swamini, please hear my humble plea, O ocean of bliss. [1]I yearn to serve your lotus feet, O Pyariju, I have no other desire. May I always remain present before you to serve you and behold your divine Raas Vilas. [2]O supremely merciful one, the very embodiment of grace, my only hope rests in you. Sri Saras Madhuri, in your shelter, prays—please grant me residence in the sacred Nikunj (secluded groves of Vrindavan). [3]

title: Taji Ke Sab Pauras Prabal Maane Tan Gun Heen -  Shri Priyadas Ji, Rasik Mohini (6)
sanskrit_text: Taji Ke Sab Pauras Prabal, Maanen Tan Gun Heen.Base Nirantar Vipin Mein, Jyon Jal Jeevan Meen.- Shri Priyadas Ji, Rasik Mohini (6)One should renounce all sense of strength and ego, considering oneself devoid of virtues and helpless. In this way, one must always reside in Shri Dham Vrindavan, just as a fish forever dwells in water.

title: Brahmapuri Shiva Ju Ki Puri - Shri Nagridas Ji (Maharaj Sawant Singh), Shri Nagridas Ji Ki Vani, Chootak Kavitt (86)
sanskrit_text: (Savaiya)Brahmapuri Shiva Ju Ki Puri, Aru Indrapuri Hu Kaha Jiya Dharaum. [1]Deva Adevana Ki Je Puri, Puni Nagapuri Mukha Taim Na Nikaraum. [2]Auru Puri Bhuva-mandala Ki, Tinake Saba Kitekahu.n Namva Ucharaum. [3]Nagara Ye Ju Kahi So Puri, Saba Gokula Ravara Upara Varaum. [4]- Shri Nagridas Ji (Maharaj Sawant Singh), Shri Nagridas Ji Ki Vani, Chootak Kavitt (86)Why should Brahmapurī (the abode of Brahmā), Kailāśa (the abode of Lord Śiva), or even the celestial realms of Indra dwell within my heart? [1]The abodes of gods, demons, and serpents—these hold no place in my desire. [2]Nor do I care to even utter the names of other exalted abodes scattered across the earth. [3]Śrī Nāgrīdāsa says, "All these realms pale before the divine splendor of Gokula and can be sacrificed upon it." [4]

title: Mandal Raas Rachyau Bimal Nirtati Kunwari Sujan - Shri Vanshi Ali, Sri Radhika Maharas, Doha (10)
sanskrit_text: Mandal Raas Rachyau Bimal, Nirtati Kunwari Sujan.Brajbala Mili Sukh Badhyau, Sab Ban Vaarat Praan.- Shri Vanshi Ali, Sri Radhika Maharas, Doha (10)When Shri Radha, the queen of divine love, performed Raas dance in the sacred Raas Mandala, with each gopi, the Braj gopis were immersed in the supreme ocean of bliss. sanskrit_text: (Kavitt)Aaj Sakhi Sevakunj Kunjan Te Aavat Ju,Praan Pyaro Preetam Ke, Sang Sukhdaayi Ju. [1]Madhur-Madhur Karen Baat, Mand Muskaay Jaat,Ras Sarasay Aat, Preeti Man Bhaayi Ju. [2]Aisi Albeli Pyaari, Shyama Sukhadhama Nyari,Kaun Bhaag Sakhi Aaj, Nainan Lakhaayi Ju. [3]Shri Gopalhit, Har Liyo Chitt-Vitt,Sharan! Chhodi Jaaun Kit, Kripa Barsayi Ju. [4]- Shri Hita Gopal Das [Of Sewa Kunj], Nikunj Ras Vallari (96)O Sākhī! Look, today Śrī Rādhā Pyārījū is emerging from the dense bowers of Sevākuṃja, showering nectar of love and bliss alongside Her beloved Śrī Kṛṣṇa. [1]Her sweet talks and playful laughter fill the heart with joy, and the shower of Her divine love has pleased my mind. [2]How blessed is this day, that these eyes have been graced with the divine vision of Albelī Sarkār, Śrī Rādhā Pyārījū, the very embodiment of love‑bliss! [3]Śrī Hit Gopāl Dās Jī declares, ‘Having glimpsed the divine beauty of Śrī Rādhā, my heart has been forever stolen, and now, I can never dream of leaving Her sacred refuge’. [4]

title: Yah Ras Rasikan Ke Liye - Shri Premdas Ji [Brother of Shri Lal Balbir Ji], Shri Premdas Ji Ki Vani (106)
sanskrit_text: Yah Ras Rasikan Ke Liye, Rasikhi Ras Barsant.Rasik Jauhari Ras Ratan, Rasikan Hi Pai Basant.- Shri Premdas Ji [Brother of Shri Lal Balbir Ji], Shri Premdas Ji Ki Vani (106)This divine nectar of the divine couple Sri Radha Krishn, flows only for Rasikas, to whom the secrets of rasa are revealed. title: Lalit Basant Saghan Vrindavan - Shri Radha Prasad Dev Ju

[2]- Shri Radha Prasad Dev JuIn the splendid spring season, the lush forests of Vrindavan bloom with joy as the vines sway gracefully. New buds and many colorful flowers blossom, while lotuses and bees indulge in their sweet play. Shri Radhikaprasad says that Lalita and the other sakhis delight, engaging in various loving services. [2]

title: Priya Charan Soun Bhai Hai - Shri Ananya Ali, Shri Ananya Ali Ji Ki Vani, Shri Vrindavan Vaas Avastha (2.38)
sanskrit_text: Priya Charan Soun Bhai Hai, Ankit Avani Rasaal.So Raj Bandat Rasik Piya, Lotat Karat Nihaal.- Shri Ananya Ali, Shri Ananya Ali Ji Ki Vani, Shri Vrindavan Vaas Avastha (2.38)The sacred land of Shri Dham Vrindavan, adorned with the footprints of Shri Priya Ji (Shri Radha), is supremely blissful. Even Lord Shri Krishna, the crown jewel among Rasikas, humbly bows to its sacred dust and is immersed in divine love bliss as He rolls upon it.

title: Hoi Ananya Bhajai Bhagwant Hi - Shri Sundar Ji
sanskrit_text: (Sawaiya)Hoi Ananya Bhajai Bhagwant Hi,Aur Kachhu Ur Main Nahin Rakhai. [1]Devi U Dev Jahan Lag Hain,Dari Kain Tinaso Kahun Deen Na Bhakhai. [2]Jog Hu Yagya Bratadi Kriya,Tinakau Nahin Tau Supinai Abhilakhai. [3]‘Sundar’ Amrit Paan Kiyau Tab,Tau Kahi Kaun Halahal Chaakhai. [4]- Shri Sundardas JiOnly when an aspirant completely renounces all other shelters and worships the Lord with exclusive devotion does he become eligible for pure bhakti. [1]Such a devotee never turns to demigods out of fear or desire, for his heart rests in unshakable faith, devoted solely to his beloved Lord. [2]Not even in his dreams does he contemplate engaging in yoga, yajñas, pilgrimages, vows, or austerities. [3]Śrī Sundardās Jī declares that such a soul forever drinks the nectar of Hari-rasa, never tasting any other poison of desires. [4]

title: Bahu Bidhi Mardan Karen - Shri Bhagwat Rasik Ki Vani, Ananyarasikabharan Granth (11.6.3)
sanskrit_text: Bahu Bidhi Mardan Karen, Nahin Chaitanya Hoi Sab.Bhagavat Ras Ki Baat, Kaha Janai Binu Anubhav.- Shri Bhagwat Rasik, Bhagwat Rasik Ki Vani, Ananyarasikabharan Granth (11.6.3)Sri Bhagavata Rasika Ji declares that just as a lifeless body can never be revived by any medicine or external effort, so too, a monotonous heart that has never experienced rasa (nectar) remains unable to grasp its essence, regardless of explanations or teachings.

title: Chali Radha! Tokau Syam Bulavai - Shri Parmanand Das, Parmanand Sagar (1194)
sanskrit_text: (Raag Basant)Chali Radha! Tokau Syam Bulavai.Uhei Dekhi Vainu Madhure Dhuni, Tero Namhin Lai Lai Gavai. [1]Dekhau Vrindavan Ki Sobha, Thaur Thaur Drum Phule.Kokil Naad Sunat Man Anand, Bhanwar Bhramat Ras-Jhoolein. [2]Unmad Jovan Madan Kulahal, Yah Aausar Hai Neekau.‘Parmanand’ Prabhu Pratham Samagam, Milayo Bhavato Jeekau. [3]- Shri Parmanand Das, Parmanand Sagar (1194)A Sakhi says to Shri Radha, “O Shri Radhe! Come, your beloved Shyamsundar is calling you. Just see, He is melodiously singing your name through the sweet tunes of His flute.” [1]Look at the unparalleled beauty of Vrindavan! Everywhere, the trees are in full bloom, marking the complete arrival of spring. At such a time, the enchanting notes of the cuckoo’s song bring joy to the heart, and the bees, intoxicated by nectar, sway in delight. [2]This moment is exceedingly delightful and auspicious, with the air filled with youthful exuberance and love at its peak. This is the perfect moment to meet your beloved Shri Krishna, whose presence fills the heart with supreme bliss, says Sri Parmanand Das. [3]

title: Adeyam Chapi Ya Datte - Shri Vagish Shastriji, Sri Radha Naam Sudha (11)
sanskrit_text: Adeyam Chapi Ya Datte Datva Raksham Karoti Ya.Yog-Kshem-Karo Radha-Bhakta Anubhavanti Yam.- Shri Vagish Shastriji, Sri Radha Naam Sudha (11)Shri Radha, ever-merciful, grants even the most unattainable to her loving devotees (who worship Her name) and takes responsibility for their protection. She is their eternal refuge, as experienced by their devotees.

title: Dekho Dekho Braj Ki Beethini Beethini - Shri Gadadhar Bhatt Ji Ki Vani (68)
sanskrit_text: (Raag Pancham or Raag Malkosa)Dekho Dekho Braj Ki Beethini Beethini Khelat Hain Hari Hori.Geet Vichitra Kolahal Kautuk Sang Sakha Lakh Kori. [1]Aayi Jhoomi Jhoomi Jhundan Juri Aganit Gokul Gori.Tinmein Juvati Kadamb Shiromani Radha Naval Kisori. [2]Chhirakat Gwalbaal Abalan Par Booka Vadan Rori.Arun Akaas Dekhi Sandhya Bhram Puni Manasa Bhai Bauri. [3]Rapata Charan Keech Aragaja Ki Kesari Kunkum Ghori.Kahi Na Jaay Gadadhar Pai Kachhu Budhibal Mati Bhai Thori. [4]- Shri Gadadhar Bhatt Ji, Shri Gadadhar Bhatt Ji Ki Vani (68)O friend, look! In every lane of Braj, Hari is joyfully playing Holi. With sweet songs, playful laughter, and enchanting pastimes, He plays Holi with thousands of cowherds. [1]Countless groups of gopis of Gokul are arriving, swaying joyfully. Among them shines the crown jewel among them, the ever-youthful, Shri Radha Rani, accompanying them. [2]The cowherd boys sprinkle abir and gulala on the gopis’ faces, turning the sky red as if dusk had arrived early, casting a mesmerizing charm upon the mind. [3]Fragrant sandalwood-mixed colorful water and red gulal spread across the ground, causing everyone to slip and slide. Shri Gadadhar Bhatt Ji says, ‘This Holi celebration has captivated my mind, leaving me unable to describe this wondrous scene.’ [4]

title: Sri Radha Vrishbhanuja Bhaktiani Pranadhar - Braj Ke Dohe
sanskrit_text: Sri Radha Vrishbhanuja, Bhaktiani Pranadhar.Vrindavipin Viharini, Pranavon Barambar.- Braj Ke DoheO Shri Radha, the most enchanting daughter of King Vrishbhanu, you are the very life and support of your devotees. O you who engages in ‘Nitya Vihara’ (eternal love-play) in Vrindavan, I bow to you endlessly.

title: Shri Radhe Ab To Hori Aani Bani Hai - Shri Vanshi Ali Ji, Varshotsav, Basant Ke Pad (10)
sanskrit_text: Shri Radhe Ab To Hori Aani Bani HaiTum Bin Kaisen Beetat Ho. [1]Bin Leene Sudhi Eri Meri MokoBirah Dabanal Jeetati Ho. [2]Ka Saun Khelo Jay Haay HoSabson Pari Achhiti Ho. [3]Ka Saun Mukh Hansi Maadi BhidaunJay Shri Vanshi Pari Aneeti Ho. [4]- Shri Vanshi Ali Ji, Varshotsav, Basant Ke Pad (10)O Shri Radhe, the festival of Holi has arrived, but without you, my heart feels empty. How can I celebrate this joyous occasion without your presence? [1]O My Swamini, until you think of me and bestow your grace, my heart will keep burning in the vast fire of your separation. How can I bear this pain? [2]With whom should I go and play Holi? Alas! I am forgotten and ignored by all. [3]Without you, who will smile and smear colors on my face? Even fate seems unfair, cries Vanshi Ali. [4]

title: Naval Basant Naval Shri Vrindavan - Shri Bhatt Devacharya, Yugal Shatak (84)
sanskrit_text: (Doha)Nav Kishor Nav Nagari, Nav Sab Saunjaru Saaj.Nav Vrindavan Nav Kusum, Nav Basant Rituraj.(Pad) [Iktal, Raag-Basant]Naval Basant Naval Shri Vrindavan, Naval Hi Phule Phool.Naval Hi Kanh Naval Sab Gopi, Nirat Tat Ekai Tool. [1]Naval Hi Sashi Jwadi Kunkuma, Naval Hi Basan Amool.Naval Hi Chhint Bani Kesar Ki, Mentat Manmath Sool. [2]Naval Gulal Udai Rang Booka, Naval Pavan Kai Jhool.Naval Hi Baje Bajat Shri Bhatt, Kalindi Ke Kool. [3]- Shri Bhatt Devacharya, Yugal Shatak (84)(Doha)Ever-new is ‘Kishor’ (Shri Krishna), ever-new is ‘Nagari’ (Shri Radha), everything is adorned in fresh splendor.Ever-new is Vrindavan, ever-new are the blossoms, and ever-new is the king of seasons, spring (Basant).(Pada)As Basant, the king of seasons, arrives, Shri Vrindavan glows with ever-new splendor, its blossoming flowers brimming with freshness.Ever-youthful is Krishna, and ever-youthful are all the gopis, among whom Shri Vrishabhanu Nandini (Sri Radha) gracefully dances with Lalji in perfect harmony. [1]The freshness of spring is further enhanced by the newly blossomed branches of fragrant sandalwood trees. Ever-new priceless garments are adorned with fresh saffron sprays, and the ever-radiant gopis, who wear these divine attires, appear ever-new, soothing the burning pangs of love. [2]Ever-new colors of gulala (scented powder), fresh abira, and vibrant roli (vermilion) are playfully tossed into the air. Ever-fresh is the breeze swaying gently, ever-fresh is the music played in this king of seasons, Basant, on the banks of the Yamuna, says Shri Bhata Devacharya. [3]

title: Jo Moson Mosi Karo Nahi Kachhu Mohi Thaur - Shri Madhuri Das, Utkantha Madhuri (76)
sanskrit_text: Jo Moson Mosi Karo, Nahi Kachhu Mohi Thaur.Tum Ho Taisi Kijiye, Aho Rasik Sir Mor.- Shri Madhuri Das, Utkantha Madhuri (76)If you judge me according to my deeds, O Lord, then I am such a great sinner that my redemption would never be possible. Apart from you, I have no other refuge. You are supremely merciful, the one who embraces even the fallen. Therefore, O crown jewel of Rasikas, please shower your grace upon this wretched soul, as per your compassionate nature.

sanskrit_text: Hari Ras Maate Je Rahain, Tin Ko Mato Agaadh.Tribhuvan Ki Sampati ‘Daya’, Trin Sam Jaanat Saadh.- Shri Dayabai (a disciple of Shri Charan Das Ji of the Shuk sect.)Those who are immersed in the nectar of Shri Hari are beyond description. title: Sant Jan Barah Maas Basant - Jagadguru Shri Kripaluji Maharaj, Prem Ras Madira, Siddhant Madhuri (103)
sanskrit_text: Sant Jan Barah Maas Basant.Piu Piu Kahi Kahi Chhin Chhin Nishidin, Kukat Kokil Sant. [1]Kabahun Jharat Drigan Ansuva Jan, Jhar Taru - Patra Anant.Kabahun Jhumi Jhumi Madhukar Jan, Gungunat Gun Kant. [2]Kabahun Pramat Phool Sarson Jan, Phooli Phooli Harshant.Prem Basant ‘Kripalu’ Nitya Rah, Ras Sarasant Na Ant. [3]- Jagadguru Shri Kripaluji Maharaj, Prem Ras Madira, Siddhant Madhuri (103)For saints, the season of spring lasts throughout all twelve months. They continuously chant Piu Piu (“Beloved! Beloved!”) in a voice overflowing with love, much like the warbling of a cuckoo in the springtime. [1]Just as leaves fall from trees in spring, saints ceaselessly shed tears of love from their eyes. Like the humming of bees in spring, they sing the divine attributes of Shyama Shyam, swaying in the intoxication of love. [2]Much like mustard plants in full bloom during spring, saints become completely immersed in divine ecstasy, their hearts overflowing with the love of their beloved. Jagadguru Shri Kripalu Ji says that while the earthly spring season lasts only two months, the saints’ spring season of love remains forever. It always keeps them submerged in the boundless ocean of divine bliss. [3]

title: Kunjbihari Ko Basant Sakhi - Shri Swami Haridas Ji, Kelimal (99)
sanskrit_text: (Raag Gaud)Kunjbihari Kau Basant Sakhi,Chalahu Na Dekhan Jahin.Nav Ban Nav Nikunj Nav Pallav,Nav Juvatin Mili Mahin. [1]Bansi Saras Madhur Dhuni Suniyat,Phooli Ang Na Mahin.Suni Shriharidas Prem Soun Premahin,Chhirakat Chhail Chubanhin. [2]- Shri Swami Haridas Ji, Kelimal (99)Haridasi (Lalita) Sakhi says to another Sakhi - O Sakhi! Come, let us witness the Vasanta Utsav (spring festival) of the divine couple, Sri Shyama Kunjbihari. Behold how Shri Dham Vrindavan overflows with fresh waves of bliss! The bowers and groves are adorned with vibrant blossoms, and the trees and flowers have blossomed anew. In such a delightful atmosphere, Sri Shyama Shyam, surrounded by young maidens, are celebrating Vasantotsav together. [1]Hearing the sweet and intoxicating melody of His flute, an ocean of divine love swells within Priya Ji’s heart, overflowing beyond the limits of her divine form. Shri Haridasi Ji, lost in these mesmerizing glimpses, says—when Priya-Priyatam, lost in the ecstasy of love, gently touch one another, it is as if two divine embodiments of pure love are bathing each other in the nectar of their boundless affection. [2]

title: Main To Govardhan Ko Jaun Meri Veer - Shri Chandrasakhi Ji
sanskrit_text: Mai To Govardhan Ko Jaun Meri Veer, Naay Mane Mero Manua.Naay Mane Mero Manua, Naay Mane Karo Kanua.Saat Serki Karoon Kadhaaiya. [1]Mai To Santan Nyot Jimaoon Mere Veer, Naay Mane Mero Manua.Saat Kos Ki De Parikrama.Mai To Maansi Ganga Nahaaoon Mere Veer, Naay Mane Mero Manua. [2]Kund Kund Ko Achman Kar Ko.Brajraj Sheesh Chadhaoon Mere Veer, Naay Mane Mero Manua. [3]Chakleshwara Ko Darshan Kar Ko.Jeevan Safal Banao Mere Veer, Naay Mane Mero Manua. [4]Chandrasakhi Bhaj Baal Krishna Chhavi.Baar Baar Bali Jaoon Mere Veer, Naay Mane Mero Manua. [5]- Shri Chandrasakhi Ji (Braj Ke Lok Geet)O sakhi, I shall go to Govardhan, for my restless heart finds peace nowhere else. With love, I will prepare an abundance of food, offer it as bhog, and invite saints to partake, as my heart is not satisfied otherwise. [1]With unwavering faith, I shall circumambulate the sacred seven kosa path, and immerse myself in the pure waters of Mansi Ganga, for my heart will never settle otherwise. [2]I will drink water from every sacred pond, anointing my head with the divine dust of Braj, I surrender myself completely, for my heart will never settle otherwise. [3]I will seek the blessings of Chakleshwar Mahadev and fulfill my life’s purpose, for my heart will never settle otherwise. [4]Shri Chandra Sakhi Ji proclaims, “By the mercy of my Guru, Shri Hit Bal Krishna Ji, I shall surrender at Govardhan, again and again, for my heart will never settle otherwise.” [5]

With love, I will prepare an abundance of fud, offer it as bhog, and invite saints to partake, as my heart is not satisfied otherwise. [1]With unwavering faith, I shall circumambulate the sacred seven kosa path, and immerse myself in the pure waters of Mansi Ganga, for my heart will never settle otherwise. [2]I will drink water from every sacred pond, anointing my head with the divine dust of Braj, I surrender myself completely, for my heart will never settle otherwise. [3]I will sik the blessings of Chakleshwar Mahadev and fulfill my life’s purpose, for my heart will never settle otherwise. [4]Shri Chandra Sakhi Ji proclaims, “By the mercy of my Guru, Shri Hit Bal Krishna Ji, I shall surrender at Govardhan, again and again, for my heart will never settle otherwise.” [5]
author: Braj Rasik Heritage

title: Rom Romni Arujhi Vilasat Kamini -  Shri Lalitmohini Dev, Ras Ke Pad (49)
sanskrit_text: Rom-Romni Arujhi Vilasat Kamini.Tan Mein Tan, Man Mein Man Basi Rahe, Ras Baadhyo Sukh Jamini. [1]Gavat Sab Sur Taar Milin Ras, Vihansat Hansat Prakas Swamini.Shri Lalita Mohini Yah Chhavi Johani, Khelau Hansau Sukh Dham Dhamini. [2]- Shri Lalitmohini Dev, Shri Lalitmohini Dev Ju Ki Vani, Rasa Ke Pada (49)Both the beloveds (Shri Radha and Shri Krishna), filled with divine love and desire, engage in such playful pastimes that their very hairs become entangled with one another. Their forms are deeply merged, and they are inseparably settled in each other’s hearts. On this blissful night, a flood of divine nectar overflows. [1]When Swamini (Shri Kishori Ji) smiles, the beauty of her divine face shines even more brilliantly. All the sakhis sing of this bliss in perfect harmony with rhythm and melody. Shri Lalitmohini Ji says, ‘O abodes of happiness, divine couple, may you both forever continue to smile and play like this endlessly.’ [2]

title: Sundar Sujan Par Mand Muskan Par - Shri Wahid Ali Ji

[2]Bhaunhen Dhan Maan Par, Lone Yug Nain Par,Prem Bhare Bain Par, “Wahid” Pagi Rahai. [3]Chanchal Vaa Tan Par, Sanware Badan Par,Nand Ke Nandan Par, Lagan Lagi Rahai. [3]May my heart forever remain devoted to Nanda's son, Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who has a playful form and a dark, radiant face. [4]

title: Yasya Kreedam Chandrama Devapatnyo - Atharva Veda, Sri Radhika Tapani Upnishad (8)
sanskrit_text: Yasya Kreedam Chandrama Devapatnyo Drishtva Nagna Atmano Na Smaranti.Vrindaranye Sthavara Jangamashcha Bhavavishtam Radhika Tam Namamah.- Atharva Veda, Sri Radhika Tapani Upnishad (8)Upon witnessing Her love-play, the moon and celestial maidens become so mesmerized that they forget their very existence. When She performs Her divine pastimes in the sacred land of Shri Vrindavan, the immovable beings begin to move, while the moving ones become still in ecstasy. I offer my salutations to such Shri Radhika.

title: Mudit Lal Pyari Charan Chitra Kare - Shri Hita Krishn Chandra
sanskrit_text: Mudit Lal Pyari Charan Chitra Kare.Neel Kamal Kar Peet Pad Padam, Char Jalaj Drig Neh Bhare. [1]Komal Piy Parasit Najuk Priya, Ur Antar Anurag Dhare.Mor Peeth Bhari Surang Tulika, Sahajhi Chhap Vichitra Dhare. [2]Param Sukhi Ya Avasar Payen, Charan Sanwari Nahu Man Hare.Krishna Chandra Radha Charan Dasi Chhabi, Sukhad Keli Rachi Chitt Are. [3]- Shri Hita Krishn ChandraThe joyful Beloved (Sri Krishn) paints Pyariju’s (Sri Radha’s) feet.With His blue lotus-like hands, He decorates the golden lotus-like feet of Sri Radha, His tear-filled eyes brimming with love. [1]As His delicate hands touch the tender feet of Sri Radha, the depths of Her heart overflow with love.Taking a peacock feather dipped in red color, She effortlessly imprints intricate designs upon them. [2]Blessed by the fortune of this supreme moment, He finds endless joy in serving Radha’s feet. Shri Krishna Chandra, the eternal servant of Her lotus feet, remains absorbed in this divine pastime of love. [3]

title: Ja Din Te Muskani Chubhi Chit - Shri Raskhan, Raskhan Ratnavali
sanskrit_text: (Sawaiya)Ja Din Te Muskani Chubhi Chit,Ta Din Te Nikasi Na Nikari. [1]Kundal Lol Kapol Maha Chhabi,Kunjan Te Nikasyo Sukhkari. [2]Haun Sakhi Aavat Hi Dagren,Pag Paind Taji Rijhai Banwari. [3]‘Raskhani’ Pari Muskani Ke Panani,Kaun Ganai Kulkaani Bichari. [4]- Sri RaskhanA sakhi says to Her friend—O friend! Ever since Śrī Kṛṣṇa's sweet smile wounded my heart, I have been unable to forget it. [1]The blissful Śrī Kṛṣṇa, playfully moving His earrings against His cheeks, suddenly emerged from the bowers of Braj. [2]O friend, I was walking on my path, but completely captivated by that forest dweller (Kṛṣṇa), I lost my way. [3]Śrī Raskhān says, 'Now I am trapped in the snare of His smile. In such a state, how can I uphold the sense of social modesty and family decorum?' [4]

title: Bhatkayau Bahu Bidhi Jag Bipin - Shri Bhartendu Harishchandra, Bhartendu Granthawali, Bhakta Sarvasva (5)
sanskrit_text: Bhatkayau Bahu Bidhi Jag Bipin, Milyo Na Kahun Vishram.Ab Anandit Hwai Rahyau, Pai Charan Ghanasyam.- Shri Bhartendu Harishchandra, Bhartendu Granthawali, Bhakta Sarvasva (5)I wandered endlessly through the dense forest of the material world, seeking rest but finding none.
